• Master in Information Systems or what corresponds. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Solid, documented expertise in sociotechnical perspective
• Solid, documented expertise in qualitative research methods
• Good fluency in English, orally and written
• The quality and relevance of the project outline (see details below) will be an important part of the overall assessment of candidates. 
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty’s PhD programme in Computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria

To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to:

Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.

As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary.

The Department of Computer Science (IDI) at NTNU in Trondheim has a vacancy for a PhD Candidate in machine learning (four-year position). The topic of the PhD is machine learning for temporal and spatiotemporal data, that is, time series, including multivariate time series observed on the nodes and edges of a graph, with a focus on forecasting and on detecting disruptions. The position is part of STRIDE, an interdisciplinary NTNU project on the resilience of transport systems (see About the project), and transport networks are the main testbed.

Forecasting models are usually trained on data from normal operating conditions. When a disruption, such as a closed link, a capacity limit or a sudden change in demand, moves a network into a regime that is rare or absent in the training data, their performance degrades, and such events are often too rare to learn from directly. The PhD will develop deep learning methods that forecast reliably under this kind of distribution shift, and that can detect and locate disruptions from the observed data.

Possible research directions include:

• time-series foundation models, including pretraining on synthetic data from simulated dynamical systems, to handle events that are rare in real data
• spatiotemporal graph neural networks that model how disruptions propagate through a network
• anomaly detection and localization of disruptions in time series on graphs
The exact research focus will be defined together with the candidate. We expect the results to be published at leading machine learning conferences and journals.

The main supervisor will be Associate Professor Massimiliano Ruocco, with co-supervisors from the STRIDE team.

About the position
We invite applications for a PhD Research Fellow position in Planetary Atmospheric Chemistry utilizing Quantum Chemistry, available at Department of Chemistry, theoretical chemistry section.

Starting date as soon as possible and no later than 01.03.2027 . The fellowship period is three years.

A fourth year maybe considered and it will involve 25 percent of other career-promoting work. Other career-promoting work may consist of teaching, supervision, and/or research assistance. This is dependent upon the qualification of the applicant and the current needs of the department.

No one can be appointed for more than one PhD Research Fellowship period at the University of Oslo. 

Place of work is The Life Science Building at Blindern, Oslo.
Project description
A PhD position is available at the Section for Theoretical Chemistry, Department of Chemistry, University of Oslo, within the project Molecular Atmospheric Chemistry on Alien Worlds (MACAW), funded by the Research Council of Norway.In this project we will employ quantum chemistry methods using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to study chemical reactions, photochemistry, identify spectral signatures for potential detection and elucidate condensation mechanisms for molecules in atmospheres beyond that of contemporary Earth. The project has a particular focus on Sulfur and Chlorine chemistry as well as isotopic fractionation processes.The successful applicant will have freedom to pursue specific research topics within the relatively wide project framework, in coordination with the supervisor. The work is first and foremost computational utilizing electronic structure methods to qualitatively study photochemical and thermal reaction mechanisms, as well as quantify reaction rates, UV-Vis spectra and other molecular properties relevant to studying the role of molecules in planetary atmospheres.
 
The work has a high degree of international collaboration within the main project supervisors' network currently spanning four continents among seven nations. This is to ensure maximal dissemination and impact of the project results, and thus the project will likely involve more than a usual amount of both hosting international visitors and travel to visit our collaborators.The project work is highly flexible, allowing the successful candidate to structure their own work.This project is an excellent opportunity for a prospective PhD candidate to make original and foundational contributions to the field of planetary atmospheric chemistry, with the potential for leading to groundbreaking discoveries of new molecules or chemical processes on other planets.
What skills are important in this role?
The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences has a strategic ambition to be among Europe’s leading communities for research, education and innovation. Candidates for these fellowships will be selected in accordance with this, and expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials.

• Fluent oral and written communication skills in English.

• Experience with quantum chemistry calculations
• Experience with scripting or programming (e.g. Python, Bash, Matlab, Fortran), and high-performance computing 
Desired qualifications:

• Experience in electronic structure methods, e.g. DFT, coupled cluster or multireference methods
• Background in chemical kinetics, reaction mechanisms, photochemistry, spectroscopy, transition state theory, atmospheric chemistry and/or physical chemistry
• Any insights into planetary/exoplanetary science and photochemical atmospheric modeling 
Language requirement:

• Good oral and written communication skills in English
• English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/ EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements:https://www.mn.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/regulations.html#toc8

• The average grade point for courses included in the Master’s degree must be B or better in the Norwegian educational system
• The Master’s thesis must have the grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system
For more information see:

The purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree.

jobs.occupation: Facility Technical Sr. Manager
jobs.description:
About Nordscale
Nordscale is the specialist operator for mission-critical AI data centers. We manage the operations that keep AI compute sites running reliably, efficiently, and safely. Founded as a strategic partnership between the AI hyperscaler Nscale and Norwegian energy company Nordkraft, we harness local expertise and data center operations experience to deliver service excellence to our customers, while building skilled local jobs and partnering with Norwegian businesses to create lasting value in the regions where we work.

 

Our culture combines local Northern Norwegian values, international expertise, and disciplined operational excellence. We’re a team built on trust, ownership, and collaboration: we communicate openly, take accountability for outcomes, and work as one team across sites, partners, and functions to deliver performance people can depend on.

 
About the Role (Job Purpose)
As Facility Technical Senior Manager, you will lead the technical MEP unit at Kvandal South outside Narvik, one of the largest AI data-centre projects in Europe. You will be central in building the unit ahead of the start of operations. You will make sure the facility’s electrical, mechanical, cooling, automation and cabling infrastructure is operated, maintained and developed safely and reliably.

 

You will report to the Facility Director and lead through an Associate Facility Technical Manager, shift managers, a project manager, technical specialists and operational support functions. Additionally, you will hold technical authority within the unit.

 

 
What You’ll be Doing (Responsibilities)
• Recruit and build the unit. Establish a structured training programme and knowledge transfer to the full technical operations team.
• Lead technical operations around the clock, ensure adequate staffing and the right mix of competencies across all shifts to support 24/7 operations.
• Manage preventive and corrective maintenance, and lead the technical response and fault-finding during critical incidents.
• Participate in testing, commissioning and handover of technical installations together with Nscale. Lead the development and implementation of technical operating procedures (SOP/MOP/EOP) and governance structures, and establish technical supplier agreements.
• Ensure safe working methods and full HSE compliance, and manage technical suppliers and contractors on quality, documentation, performance and cost.
 
About You (Skills, Qualifications & Experience)
You may come from data centres, hyperscale or HPC facilities. You may also come from technical or production leadership in continuous process industry, metallurgy, pulp and paper, power generation, offshore, maritime operations or technical defence environments. A career path from an electrical, automation or mechanical specialist role into technical or maintenance leadership is particularly valuable.

You enjoy developing people, share knowledge patiently and build ownership of procedures. You drive continuous improvement through structured processes, not by departing from them.

 

Key Characteristics

• Structured and systematic, thriving where structures, roles and requirements are clearly defined.
• Acts in compliance with procedures, standards and regulatory requirements, and holds others to the same standard.
• Resilient under pressure, building relationships of trust and finding pragmatic, holistic solutions.
 

Skills & Qualifications

• Solid experience leading the operation and maintenance of complex electrical, mechanical and cooling infrastructure, with the technical depth to challenge specialists and suppliers.
• Experience leading and developing multidisciplinary technical teams, preferably with both day and shift teams.
• Experience with procedures, work permits, safe isolation, change management and supplier management. Experience from testing, commissioning and handover is an advantage.
• Fluent English and a Scandinavian language, written and spoken. A degree in electrical, mechanical or automation engineering, or equivalent documented engineering background, is preferred.
 
What We Can Offer You
• Competitive salary negotiable based on experience. 
• Performance-based bonus tied to results and company performance. 
• The chance to build the technical organisation, procedures and training from the ground up, and to bring Kvandal South’s technical systems into operation in 2027.
• Relocation support assessed individually, if required. 
 
Equal Opportunities Statement
We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse, and equitable workplace. We believe that a variety of perspectives enriches our work environment, and we encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities.  We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

 

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.

jobs.occupation: 1352 Postdoctoral position in marine ecological modelling
jobs.description:
About the Position
The Institute of Marine Research (IMR) offers a 3-year postdoctoral position as part of the MORSE (“Models supporting practical restoration of habitats and species in Europe’s seas”) research project funded by Horizon Europe. This project sits within IMR’s strategic initiative to build a strong center for marine research within one of Europe's largest marine research institutes. The candidate will ideally start in early 2027. 

We seek a postdoctoral researcher with a background in ecological modelling, with relevant experience and publication record on modelling marine and/or aquatic ecosystems. The postdoctoral researcher will work across several work packages, including WP5 (reviewing and compiling data on restoration pathways, pressures, and ecological needs of focal species and habitats, and defining favourable reference areas), WP6 (species distribution modelling and assessment of environmental status (NEAT), WP7 (modelling land-, and sea-based pressures, and MPAs), and WP8 (modelling ecosystem services). The broader aim of the project is to develop and demonstrate effective and climate-resilient restoration models for European marine ecosystems to inform more effective restoration efforts. 

The postdoctoral researcher will work with a team of researchers at IMR and collaborating partners to carry out and deliver research outcomes in the MORSE project. The MORSE project that the postdoctoral position is associated with is a 4-year project that is led by the Finnish Environmental Institute (SYKE) and includes institutions across seven European countries (Finland, Sweden, Norway, UK, Spain, Portugal, and Greece). Travel to workshops and meetings in these countries should be anticipated. The postdoctoral researcher will gain mentoring support, training, and networking opportunities from the leading researchers associated with the MORSE project, and have the opportunity to establish connections and advance their research career over the course of the project. More information about MORSE can be found at the project website: https://morse-project.eu/ 

Knowledge about northern European marine ecosystems is an advantage, as the postdoctoral researcher will be responsible for modelling Norwegian marine ecosystems. The position is placed within the Benthic Communities research group and can be located at any of the IMR offices. Note that the IMR project lead (Karine Gagnon) is based at Flødevigen Research Station, but the research group includes members across all three locations. IMR has good links and cooperation with industry, management, and the university sector. We offer the opportunity to be part of a collaborative, interdisciplinary, and ambitious research group with strong national and international links.

Main tasks:

• Lead and support MORSE research activities as directed by project leaders. 
• Write research publications, reports, and grant proposals.
• Participate in scientific conferences, science communication, and outreach activities. 
• Review and compile existing data on restoration pathways, ecosystem status, and pressures for focal species and habitats, and define favourable reference areas for these 
• Review and compile existing models and data sources for the Norwegian sea areas (including the Skagerrak, Norwegian Sea, North Sea, and Barents Sea) 
• Apply species distribution models and assess environmental status using the NEAT tool 
• Model land-based and sea-based pressures on marine habitats, and the role of MPAs 
• Model climate scenarios and ecosystem services 
• Participate in work package coordination and reporting 
• Maintain and curate datasets and coordinate data sharing and modelling efforts across MORSE partners.About the Research Group and Our Work
The Benthic Communities group focuses on research, mapping, and monitoring of benthic ecosystems, including seagrass meadows, macroalgae forests, and deep-sea ecosystems. Research within the project will support IMR’s national advisory task on ecosystem-based management of seas and coastal areas, where environmental changes and human activities and are important factors. The research group has over 30 employees base on Flødevigen, Bergen, and Tromsø.
Qualification Requirements
For this position, we are looking for a candidate with

• PhD in biology or ecology, preferably with a focus on ecological modelling
• Documented experience in ecological modelling 
• Strong publication record in international peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and oral skills in English
The working language at the Institute of Marine Research is Norwegian. Being able to communicate well in Norwegian is an important prerequisite for both the employee and our institute. We expect non-Norwegian-speaking employees to complete Norwegian language courses during the first two years of employment. The institute will cover the cost of completed and passed Norwegian courses.
Personal Qualities
At the Institute of Marine Research, we believe that personality plays a role in how one works, communicates, and thrives in the workplace. For this position, we are looking for a colleague who

• Good communication and collaboration skills. 
• Good organisational and logistics skills. 
• Ability to complete work on time and meeting deadline 
• Ability to work efficiently independently and in teams.Desired Qualifications
• Strong skills and experience in ecological modelling and data analysis
• Ability and willingness to collaborate with colleagues in Norway and abroad 
• Ability and willingness to organize and lead joint modelling efforts with partners abroad 
• Research experience in marine ecosystems, species, and habitats 
• Research experience in ecological restoration and/or conservationInclusion and Diversity is a Strength
The Institute of Marine Research believes that inclusion and diversity are strengths. Therefore, we encourage all qualified candidates to apply for a position with us, regardless of age, gender, disability, nationality, or ethnic background. The Institute is an Inclusive Workplace (IA) company, and we aim to accommodate applicants with disabilities.

If there are qualified applicants with disabilities, employment gaps, or immigrant backgrounds, we will invite at least one applicant from each of these groups to an interview. To be considered for affirmative action, you must meet the requirements and indicate that you wish to be considered for the action in your application. You can read more here.
Your application must include 
• a cover letter describing your research interests and motivation for applying for the position. The letter should not exceed one A4 page.• Full name and contact details for two or three referees, preferably your PhD supervisor and/or references from recent employment.• CV, transcripts, diplomas, and relevant certificates.• A list of scientific publications, if applicable.

All documents must be in a Scandinavian language or in English. Candidates with documentation from foreign institutions must include an explanation of the institution’s grading system.
We offer
• the opportunity to work in one of Europe’s leading marine research institutes
• a creative working environment
• facilities in either Flødevigen, Bergen or Tromsø 
• flexible work hours 
• public sector occupational pension through the Norwegian Public Service Pension Funds (SPK)
• access to company cabins, fitness facilities, and other welfare benefitsAditional information
The position is remunerated as 1352 Postdoctoral in accordance with the main collective agreement in the state sector, depending on your qualifications and the characteristics of the position. A 2 % contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted from the salary.

Applications must be submitted electronically via Jobbnorge.

Please note that information about applicants may be made public even if the applicant has requested not to be listed. Applicants will be informed in advance if such disclosure is necessary.

The Institute of Marine Research is subject to export control regulations. These regulations apply to the processing of applications for the position.

Applicants with education from abroad may be asked to provide NOKUT approval of their qualifications. You may be asked to approve that the Institute of Marine Research conducts a background check.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The Institute of Marine Research is one of Europe’s largest marine research institutes, with over 1,000 employees and a range of high-standard research facilities and laboratories. Our main activities are research, advisory work, and monitoring. The institute owns and operates eight research vessels. Our headquarters are in Bergen, with additional offices in Tromsø and research stations in Matre, Austevoll, and Flødevigen.The Institute of Marine Research aims to be a leading provider of knowledge to ensure the sustainable management of marine ecosystem resources—nationally and internationally—across the entire value chain from ocean to food, including the marine environment, fish nutrition, and safe, healthy seafood.

jobs.occupation: PhD position in Aluminium Extrusion
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MTP) at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) has a vacancy for a PhD candidate within aluminium extrusion, associated with the Centre for Research-based Innovation SFI FAST – Future Aluminium Structures.

The position is a  3-year doctoral research fellowship starting in 2026. The PhD candidate will be embedded in the forming research activities of SFI FAST  and will work closely with NTNU, SINTEF, and leading international industrial partners in the aluminium value chain (Hydro, Benteler Automotive, Raufoss Technology, Speira, Raufoss Aluminium, Renault, etc).

This PhD position focuses on aluminium extrusion of profiles based on high recycled content. The research will address process–microstructure–property relationships, weld integrity, die design, and product quality in extrusion of complex profiles from post-consumer scrap aluminium (PCS).

The use of PCS in the production of structural components (i.e. automotive) is currently limited but is expected to grow as more stringent sustainability requirements and regulations come into effect. The candidate will establish and validate numerical forming simulations, predict PCS effects on seam- and charge weld quality, surface quality, integrate microstructure and texture evolution into the models, integrate quenching sequence in modelling, conduct industrial experiments, and demonstrate validity through use-cases in the project. The foci of the research work include practical experiments (including extrusion experiments, and mechanical/microstructure characterization tests), theoretical analysis, and numerical simulation. 

The candidate will work in collaboration with industrial partners and needs to be responsible for reporting progress and delivering outputs to the FAST centre. S/he will have the possibility to obtain a cotutelle (‘dual’) PhD degree between NTNU and University of Bologna, Italy.
About SFI FAST – Future Aluminium Structures
SFI FAST (Future Aluminium Structures) is a national Centre for Research-based Innovation (SFI) funded by the Research Council of Norway and the aluminum industry. The centre is led by NTNU in close collaboration with SINTEF and a broad consortium of 16 leading industrial partners across the aluminium value chain. FAST runs from 2026 to 2033 and represents one of Norway’s most ambitious long-term research initiatives within aluminium materials, manufacturing technologies, and circular economy.

The primary objective of FAST is to establish the scientific and technological knowledge base required to enable the large-scale use of post-consumer scrap (PCS) aluminium in high-value, structural, and safety-critical products. FAST adopts a through-scale and through-process research methodology, integrating materials science, manufacturing processes, product and structural design, and lifecycle performance.

A key outcome of FAST is the development of the FAST Virtual Lab, a digital framework combining experimental data, physics-based models, and data-driven methods to support design, manufacturing, and decision-making across aluminium value chains.

Education and competence building are central pillars of FAST. The centre will educate more than 18 PhD and postdoctoral researchers and over 100 MSc students, strengthening Norway’s international position in aluminium research and innovation. The two positions posted here will be among the first ones to start in the center. 
Duties of the position
• Study, prototype and validate extrusion processes mechanisms for improved accuracy and mechanical properties
• Investigate the impact of thermal-mechanical processing on the subsequent forming processes and end-product quality
• Perform mechanical and microstructural testing, characterization and analysis to assess the properties of material and components
• Investigate the process behaviours, mechanisms and models to improve and optimize the process capabilities
• Conduct and publish high-level research at peer-reviewed journals and international conferences
• Work closely with industry and employ the industry-as-laboratory concept for extrusion trials and studies
• Participate and contribute to research group and FAST WP3 (Forming) activities, including mentoring and supervising MScs
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Materials Science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Strong academic background relevant to metal forming or aluminium processing
• You must have experience in continuum-based modelling using FEA software
• Good written and oral English skills
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Knowledge and testing skills in material characterization and microstructural analysis of aluminium alloys, using advance equipment like SEM, TEM, P-FIB, etc.
• Experience in the design and development of machine tools in metal forming processes
• Experience in using alternative, relevant modelling methods for material, process, and product behaviour (like using analytical, data-driven modelling approaches, AI, etc.)
• Background from or knowing the NTNU/Norwegian  or University of Bologna university system to be prepared for following the mandatory exchange path associated with a cotutelle PhD degree
• Experience with industrial research and industry-as-a-laboratory type of activitiesPersonal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Highly motivated
• Able to work independently
• Curious and enthusiastic
• Strong ability to systematically carry out goal-oriented work
• Enjoy and contribute to interdisciplinary research
• Keen interest in learning and working in teams
• Good skills to deliver oral and written presentation of research results
• Strong interest in combining theory and practice through experimental and numerical research
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• Exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow position in Mathematics
jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a PhD Research Fellow position in Mathematics, available at the Department of Mathematics, as part of QSTAR – Centre for quantum computing and applications.

Starting date as soon as possible and no later than 01.04.2027.

The fellowship period is three years.

A fourth year may be considered, and it will involve 25 % of other career-promoting work. Other career-promoting work may consist of teaching, supervision, and/or research assistance. This is dependent upon the qualifications of the applicant and the current needs of the department.

No one can be appointed for more than one PhD Research Fellowship period at the University of Oslo.

Place of work is Department of Mathematics/QSTAR at Blindern, Oslo.
Job description
The position is affiliated with QSTAR - Centre for Quantum Computing and Applications. QSTAR is a five-year research centre funded by the Research Council of Norway (project number 361617) and hosted and led by SINTEF. It brings together researchers at SINTEF, UiO, NTNU, OsloMet and Simula Research Laboratory, with international partners at the University of Copenhagen and RISE in Sweden.

The centre connects four research work packages: fault tolerance and error correction; compilation and Hamiltonian engineering; foundations of quantum algorithms; and quantum algorithms for applications. Together, they address how quantum information can be protected, how algorithms can be implemented, and where quantum computation may offer advantages, particularly in chemistry and optimisation.

PhD candidates become part of a research community spanning mathematics, physics, chemistry and optimisation. The centre’s programme includes seminars, PhD schools, annual retreats and conferences, alongside opportunities for international exchange and collaboration across partner institutions.

Learn more about the centre’s research, people and activities on the QSTAR website

The position is advertised within work package 1 “Fault-tolerance and error correction”. More specifically, the successful candidate will work on theoretical questions in one of the following two projects.
 
The first project studies questions in the fields of quantum groups and tensor categories, with a particular focus on possible applications to fault-tolerant quantum computation through the paradigm of topological quantum computation. We also aim to develop and extend connections between these fields and quantum information science in a broad sense, beyond fault-tolerance.

The second project is concerned with employing methods of group theory, representation theory and operator algebras to construct new families of quantum codes with improved performance and novel features. Another core task in the second project will be to study various families of quantum channels from the perspective of quantifying noise.

The PhD Fellow will join the Operator Algebra group in Section 6 at the Department of Mathematics, where the work will be conducted in close collaboration with other members of the QSTAR project.

The PhD Fellow will:

• Look for application of the theory of tensor category and quantum groups to problems related to topological quantum computation.
• Look for connections between quantum information theory and noncommutative geometry through studying quantum channels as noise models.
• Work in close collaboration with researchers in operator algebras and quantum information theory.
• Join a research group with broad expertise in mathematics, quantum chemistry, and theoretical physics.What skills are important in this role?
The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences has a strategic ambition to be among Europe’s leading communities for research, education and innovation. Candidates for these fellowships will be selected in accordance with this, and expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials.

Required qualifications:

• Master’s degree or equivalent in Mathematics or Physics. Foreign completed degree (M.Sc.-level) corresponding to a minimum of four years in the Norwegian educational system
• Relevant experience in operator algebras, representation theory, or quantum information theory
• For applicants with an MSc in Physics, a solid mathematical component in their education is required.
• Fluent oral and written communication skills in English.
Candidates without a master’s degree have until 31.03.2027 to complete the final exam.

Desired qualifications:

• Documented, sound knowledge of one or more of the following topics: C*-algebras, noncommutative geometry, representation theory and its applications to quantum groups, quantum field theory, quantum information theory
• Fluent oral and written communication skills in a Scandinavian language
Language requirement:

• Good oral and written communication skills in English
• English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/ EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements:https://www.mn.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/regulations.html#toc8
Grade requirements:The norm is as follows:

• The average grade point for courses included in the Bachelor’s degree must be C or better in the Norwegian educational system
• The average grade point for courses included in the Master’s degree must be B or better in the Norwegian educational system
• The Master’s thesis must have the grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system
For more information see:

The purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. 
What are we looking for in you?
Personal skills:

• Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
• Ability to work precise in a structured manner and swiftly adapts to new tasks
• Good communication and collaboration skills
• Positive attitude and the ability to handle hectic periods
Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal qualifications.
We can offer you
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
• A pleasant and stimulating work environment
• Good welfare schemes
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities
• Career development programmes
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes
• Oslo’s family-friendly surroundings with their rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities
• Salary in position as PhD Research Fellow, position code 1017 in salary range NOK from 550 800 - 595 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund We need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. We hope you will apply for the position with us.
How to apply
The application must include:

• Cover letter (statement of motivation, summarizing scientific work and research interest) of maximum length 2 A4 pages.
• CV (summarizing education, positions and academic work - scientific publications, administrative experience and other qualifying activity)
• Copies of the original Bachelor and Master’s degree diploma and transcripts of records
• Letters of recommendation: these are not to be submitted with the application, but may be requested later during the evaluation process
• Documentation of English Language requirements. The appointed candidate cannot start in the position until approved documentation of English language proficiency has been submitted.
• List of publications and academic work that the applicant wishes to be considered by the evaluation committee
• Names and contact details of 2-3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and telephone number)
Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".Foreign applicants should attach an official explanation of their University's grading system.

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
General information
The best qualified candidates will be invited for interviews.Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we can't, you will hear from us.
 
Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian), Guidelines concerning appointment to post doctoral and research posts at UiO (Norwegian) and Regulations for the degree of Philosophiae Doctor (PhD) at the University of Oslo.  

The University of Oslo has a transfer agreement with all employees that is intended to secure the rights to all research results etc.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. 

The Department of Mathematics is part of the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences at the University of Oslo. The Department is engaged in teaching and research covering a wide spectrum of subjects within mathematics, mechanics and statistics. The research is on theory, methods and applications. The areas represented include: fluid mechanics, biomechanics, statistics and data science, computational mathematics, combinatorics, partial differential equations, stochastics and risk, algebra, geometry, topology, operator algebras, complex analysis and logic.

We have almost 50 persons in permanent academic positions and a large number of post docs and Ph.D. students. We also have an administrative and technical staff. The department represents a leading research environment in mathematical areas in Norway, and has a highly international profile.

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in Political Science - Norway and the EU
jobs.description:
About the position 
ARENA Centre for European Studies at the University of Oslo invites applications for a position as PhD Research Fellow (SKO 1017) in political science or another relevant social science discipline. The position is for a period of three years, with no teaching or other required duties. 

The place of work is ARENA Centre for European Studies, University of Oslo.
 
ARENA is an interdisciplinary research centre at the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo. Since 1994, the centre has studied political, security, economic, legal and social integration, transformation and cooperation in Europe. ARENA has extensive experience in coordinating international research projects and networks funded by European and Norwegian institutions. 

The centre has around 30 academic and four administrative staff. More information about ARENA is available here.
More about the position 
Europe is being reshaped by war, geopolitical rivalry and a renewed enlargement agenda. As the EU's rules and decisions reach further beyond its borders, Norway faces key questions about alignment, influence and democratic control. Norway is one of the most closely integrated non-member states. That makes it an important case for understanding what it means to be part of European integration without being a member of the Union.

ARENA is looking for a PhD Research Fellow who wants to write a dissertation on Norway's relationship with the EU. The successful candidate will develop and carry out their own doctoral project in a research environment with long experience of studying European integration and its consequences for countries both inside and outside the Union.

We expect theoretically informed empirical studies and particularly welcome projects that take a comparative approach, but single-case studies of Norway are also welcome. Examples of comparisons could include comparing and contrasting Norway with other associated or third countries (such as Iceland, Switzerland or the United Kingdom), EU member states or candidate countries. Comparisons across policy areas are also welcome. We are open to a range of theoretical and methodological approaches.

Relevant research areas could include, but are not limited to:

• Norway's association model: Projects could for example address how the EEA Agreement and Norway's many other agreements with the EU shape Norwegian politics, public administration and regulation, or how they compare with those of comparable EU member or affiliated states. Projects could look at Norway's room for manoeuvre and influence vis-à-vis the EU, at questions of democratic legitimacy and control, or at how the association model is evolving as the EU changes. 
• Justice and home affairs: Projects could for example address Norway's participation in Schengen, European migration and asylum policy, border management, or police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. Projects could study how EU developments in these fields affect Norwegian policies, institutions and societal security, possibly compared with other associated or member countries.
We are looking for candidates with interesting and relevant research ideas, strong theoretical and analytical skills, and solid methodological competence. The project proposal should combine clear theoretical and empirical ambitions with a realistic and feasible research design.
Responsibilities
The appointment as a PhD Research Fellow at ARENA is for a period of three years, with no compulsory duties. As a fellow, you will be based at ARENA Centre for European Studies’ premises in Gaustadalléen, Oslo. Presence at the unit is a requirement. 

You will be admitted to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Oslo.

This is a full-time position commencing in the winter or spring of 2027. You will have access to office space, equipment, and services, as well as resources for fieldwork and conference participation as needed.
What skills are important in this role?
Required selection criteria 

• The position requires a completed master's degree equivalent to a two-year programme (120 ECTS credits) within the social sciences, approved by the faculty as a basis for admission.
• Grades placing the candidate in the top tier of the field (this also applies to the master's thesis)
• The master's degree must include relevant training in research design and methodology
• The master's thesis must correspond to a minimum workload of six months, i.e., 30 ECTS credits
• 
Excellent oral and written English proficiency is required

ARENA’s working language is English, and therefore, fluency in oral and written English is required. As Norway’s relationship with the EU is central to the position, Norwegian sources will be important, making good proficiency in Norwegian (or another Scandinavian language) an advantage.
 
Personal suitability

• You must be able to work independently and in a structured manner.

• You should possess good collaborative skills and demonstrate the ability, willingness, and commitment to contribute to the development of the research field.

• 
You should be able to take initiative and wish to participate actively in an international and interdisciplinary research team.

Appointment as a research fellow requires admission to a doctoral programme, or a binding agreement regarding admission. 

Application for admission to a PhD programme must normally be submitted within three months of the start of the research project leading to the PhD degree. 
Basis for assessment
In the assessment of candidates, particular emphasis will be placed on:

(1) the quality and relevance of the project proposal

(2) academic qualifications (transcripts must be attached)

(3) the master's thesis and any other published work

(4) references.

Personal qualities and motivation will be taken into consideration.

Potential candidates will be invited to an interview.
We need different perspectives in our work 
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will provide appropriate accommodations should you need them. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.
 
If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps, we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us. 
We can offer you

two per cent deduction is made from the salary for the mandatory contribution to the State Pension Fund.

Application

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Electrochemistry
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
We have a vacancy for a PhD Candidate at the Department of Materials Science and Engineering in the field of Electrochemistry. PhD candidates are expected to complete the degree of PhD within three or four (including teaching duties) years.

Electrochemistry is a truly interdisciplinary field drawing on chemistry, physics, materials science, electronics, and nanotechnology alike. Electrochemistry therefore offers unique possibilities for interesting scientific work and an exciting career. Electrochemistry is essential in current pursuit of the green transition and the establishing of a sustainable society, as it is critical to some pivotal technologies such as hydrogen technology (water electrolysis and fuel cells), and batteries. It is also critical to the manufacture of materials that go into a diverse set of technologies related to energy storage and renewables. The demand for staff with expertise in Electrochemistry is therefore soaring.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
The available PhD position is affiliated with the research HYDROGENi centre for hydrogen technology (https://hydrogeni.no/), one of several Centres for Environment-friendly Energy Research funded by the Norwegian Research Council and major energy and industry companies. The HYDROGENi centre constitutes a strong team of research and industry partners and globally leading universities and research centres. The PhD student will participate in a network of PhD students and industrialists across disciplines and will participate in summer and winter schools organised by the centre in addition to the training offered by the PhD programme itself. The primary objective of the PhD work will be to establish analysis tools for performance and degradation of electrocatalyst layers for alkaline electrolyte membrane water electrolysis.

The PhD student will have access to state-of-the-art equipment for manufacture and in situ characterization of performance and degradation processes in electrocatalyst layers.
Duties of the position
• Experimental electrochemistry and characterization of degradation processes (voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, chronoamperometry and others, including in-situ and in-line methods)
• Manufacture electrocatalytic layers (preparation of inks, spraying, templating techniques) and membrane-electrode-assembly for AEM water electrolysis.
• Cell assembly and in-situ single cell test station operation.
• Analysis of results
• Communicate with industry and the research community
• Scientific and technical reporting through regular dissemination channels, public dissemination through social media and other channels, and participation in international conferences and project meetings
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
• Participate actively in the research group and mentor master studentsRequired selection criteria
• You must have a professionally relevant background in (experimental) electrochemistry and nanotechnology.
• Experience in cell assembly and operation of single cell test stations.
• You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's doctoral program, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in chemistry, nanotechnology, materials science, physics or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation.
• Fluent in written and oral English.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Experience in electrochemical impedance spectroscopy.
• Experience in manufacture of electrocatalyst layers, MEAs and characterization of such.
• Experience in assembly of AEM water electrolysis cells.
• Experience in using single cell test stations.
• An ability and willingness to interact with students (teaching and supervision) students at all (five-year integrated) MSc levels will be considered an advantage.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity 
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions 
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
Evaluate and remove/add what is relevant for the position.

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work. 

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Materials Science and Engineering (https://www.ntnu.edu/studies/phmt) within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English. Examples of this could be your Master’s thesis and scientific publications.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• CV 
• Copy of Master's thesis. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page)
• Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work
• Possibly certificates
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Frode Seland, email: frode.seland@ntnu.no

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Advisor Marie Kristiansen, e-mail: marie.kristiansen@ntnu.no 

Application deadline: 16.11.2026

-----------------

For practical information about working at NTNU, please visit this webpage. 

The city of Trondheim is a modern European city with a rich cultural scene. Trondheim is the tech capital of Norway with a population of 200,000. The Norwegian welfare state, including healthcare, schools, kindergartens and overall equality, is probably the best of its kind in the world. Professional subsidized day-care for children is easily available. Furthermore, Trondheim offers great opportunities for education (including international schools) and possibilities to enjoy nature, culture and family life and has low crime rates and clean air quality.

jobs.occupation: Industrial Pipefitters – Ermeto / Hydraulic Tubing
jobs.description:
About the opportunity
We are looking for experienced Industrial Pipefitters specializing in Ermeto hydraulic tubing systems for long-term shipyard projects in Norway.

The work involves precision tube bending, hydraulic pipe assembly, installation of mechanical tube fittings and working from technical drawings.

We are particularly interested in candidates with practical experience in shipbuilding, offshore fabrication, hydraulic installations or industrial piping systems.
Your responsibilities
• Bend and prepare hydraulic tubing using Tubomat or equivalent tube-bending machines.
• Operate EO2 assembly machines or equivalent equipment for hydraulic tube connections.
• Install Ermeto fittings, compression fittings and industrial tubing systems.
• Read and interpret technical drawings and installation specifications.
• Identify different tubing materials, including alloy steel and stainless steel.
• Select appropriate fittings, components and materials independently.
• Ensure accurate installations and follow workplace safety procedures.Required qualifications
• Documented practical experience with industrial hydraulic tubing or Ermeto systems.
• Experience operating tube-bending machines.
• Familiarity with EO2 or comparable hydraulic tube-connection systems.
• Ability to read technical drawings.
• Knowledge of industrial pipe fittings and tubing materials.
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
• Basic working English preferred; English communication capability is required within each team.
Important: This position is intended for experienced industrial pipefitters, not general residential plumbing specialists.
What is offered
• Hourly salary, depending on qualifications, in accordance with Norwegian law.
• 4/2 rotational working schedule.
• Accommodation and meals covered.
• Necessary tools and equipment provided on site.
• Long-term project opportunities in the Norwegian shipbuilding industry.
• Start dates following customer approval.How to apply
Send your CV in English, including details of your previous industrial pipefitting experience.

Please specify which tube-bending machines, hydraulic connection systems and Ermeto/EO2 equipment you have used.

Selected candidates will be contacted for further screening and assessment.

jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Wargaming
jobs.description:
Do you want to contribute to the future of wargaming research in the Norwegian Armed Forces?

The Norwegian Defence Command and Staff College (Stabsskolen), part of the Norwegian Defence University College (NDUC/FHS), is seeking a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in wargaming and a desire to pursue a PhD in which wargaming plays a central role. The position is funded through the Technology in Multi-Domain Operations (TEK-MDO) project and is offered for a fixed term of four years, with 25% of the position allocated to teaching and other duties. NDUC’s long-term ambition is to establish a permanent academic capability in wargaming.

The NDUC is Norway’s leading academic institution in military power, security, and defence policy. The College delivers accredited education and advanced professional military education, conducts research related to military power and operations, and supports the Norwegian Armed Forces, NATO, and the United Nations.  The successful candidate will contribute to the planning, development, and conduct of wargaming activities at Stabsskolen, within the TEK-MDO project, and across NDUC, working closely with academic staff, military practitioners, and national and international partners. The position places particular emphasis on the use of new technologies, innovative methods, and pedagogical development in wargaming activities.

The fellowship offers a unique opportunity to contribute to establishing a long-term academic environment for wargaming at NDUC, while working closely with researchers, military practitioners, NATO partners, and other stakeholders and partners.

NDUC has campuses in Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim, and Lillehammer.

NDUC aims to be an attractive and inclusive workplace that attracts the best candidates, regardless of gender, sexual orientation, age, or ethnicity.

Work Tasks
• Conduct doctoral research and complete a PhD thesis focused on      wargaming
• Contribute to wargaming research and practice at NDUC through      publications, academic networks, and practitioner engagement
• Contribute to teaching, supervision, and other academic      activities
• Support wargaming activities and related projects, including Technology      in Multi-Domain Operations (TEK-MDO) and Applied Technology in Military      Operations (ATMO)
• Engage with national and international academic and professional networksRequired Qualifications
• A master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant discipline
• Demonstrated interest in      wargaming, game-based learning, simulation, professional military      education, defence analysis, or related fields
• Strong academic record and      demonstrated research potential
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English
• The position requires a security clearance at the level of HEMMELIG (Secret) in accordance with the Norwegian Security Act. For more information, see www.nsm.no 
Preferred qualifications:

• Experience with wargaming, simulation, tabletop exercises, or      game-based learning
• Teaching experience or an interest in the educational      applications of wargaming
• Experience from military service, particularly at the      operational level
• Understanding of military operations, as well as security- and      defence policy
• Experience with qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research
• Communication skills in Norwegian

• Self-motivated and able to work independently
• Flexible and adaptable
• Strong collaborative and interpersonal skills
• Curious, creative, and willing to explore and innovate 
• Able to manage long-term research projects and meet deadlinesWe Offer:
• A unique opportunity to help shape the development of wargaming      research and education within the Norwegian defence sector
• The opportunity to pursue a PhD while contributing directly to      the development of wargaming in military education and analysis

• While the position is offered as a four-year fixed-term      appointment, NDUC has a long-term ambition to establish a permanent      academic capability in wargaming. The successful candidate will have the      opportunity to contribute to laying the foundation for this development

A statutory deduction of 2% to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (Statens pensjonskasse) applies

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Interface-resolved CFD for boiling and condensation on engineered surfaces
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
A 3-year PhD position is available at the Department of Energy and Process Engineering as part of the HORIZON Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action (MSCA) Doctoral Network “SurPhase”. 

Efficient boiling and condensation are fundamental to thermal management in refrigeration, air conditioning, electronics cooling and energy systems. The transition towards low Global Warming Potential refrigerants is essential for reducing environmental impact, but these fluids introduce new challenges associated with altered wetting behaviour, nucleation, liquid and vapour transport, dryout and flooding. This PhD project will develop advanced CFD models for boiling and condensation on engineered surfaces. The candidate will investigate how interfacial transport and surface characteristics can be represented reliably in numerical simulations and will validate modelling approaches against experimental evidence generated within the network. 

The successful candidate will work at at the Thermal Two-Phase Flow Laboratory (http://folk.ntnu.no/fernandi/) at NTNU’s main Gløshaugen campus in Trondheim, Norway. Numerical simulations will be performed on both commercial packages and with in-house developed numerical codes. The candidate will be part of a friendly working environment, with close interaction with our postdoc, PhD and MSc candidates working in our group. The position will be supervised by Professor Maria Fernandino.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
SurPhase is a Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network training 12 doctoral candidates in surface engineering and phase-change heat transfer for low-global-warming-potential refrigerants. SurPhase brings together four academic beneficiaries: the University of Birmingham, Sabanci University, Norwegian University of Science and Technology and University of Padova, supported by Ericsson, Arçelik, Fraunhofer IFAM, ANSYS and Hexxcell. The programme combines academic and industrial research, international mobility, network-wide training and cross-sector secondments.
Duties of the position
• Develop and implement models for heat and mass transfer within diﬀuse and sharp interface methods
• Contribute to academic publications, project reports and other dissemination activities
• Participate in meetings with supervisors and colleagues
• Engage in secondments as part of the project training activities
• Participate in structured training programs and network events organized by the consortium
• Collaborate with other doctoral candidates in the consortium
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
To apply for these MSCA Training positions, applicants must fulfil the following criteria:

• At the time of recruitment by the host organisation, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in the country of the recruiting beneficiary for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding their recruitment date. 
• Applicants must be willing and able to undertake the planned international academic and industrial secondments within the SurPhase network.
General required criteria:

• You must meet the requirements for admission to the IV Faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, applied mathematics physics, applied physics, or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a Master’s thesis.
• Master students can apply, but the Master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than June 2027.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in the English language are required. 
Specific requirements for the proposed project:

• You must have an academically strong background within fluid mechanics and heat transfer, demonstrated through projects, activities, and/or theses.
• Good programming experience with Matlab, Python, C or similar.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Strong experience in CFD and numerical methods
• Experience with model verification and experimental validation
• Experience in interface-capturing or diffuse interface methods, phase-change modelling, and UDF/user coding will be considered an advantage
• Strong fundamentals in condensation and two-phase flow heat transfer will be considered an advantage
• Previous experience writing and contributing to peer-reviewed journal articles will be considered an advantagePersonal characteristics
• Enthusiastic and highly motivated
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Able to work independently and in a team
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity 
• Flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• Exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international professional environment
• A strong group of researchers focused on fluid mechanics and heat transfer
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free, optional Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

The Department of Energy and Process Engineering (EPT) has established EPT Women in Science. The group is focused on supporting female Research Assistants, PhD Candidates, Postdoctoral Fellows and permanent academic employees within the Department. This support aims to help develop the academic careers of female employees, and is also made visible to our student body, to encourage them to consider an academic path. As part of the EPT Women in Science initiative we continue to build on our international network, inviting prominent female academics within and beyond the field of Engineering to speak at our events.

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment.

The position is conditional on external funding.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above.
