jobs.description:
About the position
A fixed-term 100 % position as a PhD Research Fellow in Civil and Structural Engineering, is available at the University of Agder, Faculty of Engineering and Science. The position is affiliated with the Department of Engineering Sciences and is offered for a period of three years. The position is located at Campus Grimstad. The starting date is agreed with the Faculty.

The Department of Engineering Sciences has more than 120 employees in scientific positions and more than 1500 students at all levels. A wide range of research activities is conducted across the department’s research groups: Mechatronics, Renewable Energy, Civil Engineering, and Industrial Economy. Interdisciplinary projects within the department or with other research groups are also welcome.

This position will be affiliated with the Civil Engineering section. The department has extensive international collaboration and works closely with industrial partners and public-sector organisations in the region. These collaborations provide valuable opportunities for both teaching and research. Our partners contribute assignments, expertise and resources.

Project background

The position is associated with a recently awarded EU project, HelioSea. The project aims to develop innovative interconnected floating solar arrays for offshore sites. The project will assess innovative concepts under various environmental conditions, investigate systems integration and the co-location of different marine renewable energy devices, and conduct techno-economic analyses.
Responsibilities
The PhD research fellow will conduct research on the design and analysis of multibody floating solar systems under offshore environmental conditions. Such systems are typically characterised by lightweight floats with mechanical connectors and mooring systems.

The work will involve analytical modelling and numerical analysis of multibody hydrodynamics. Structural analysis may also be included, depending on the research focus. The candidate is expected to work collaboratively in an international research environment.

The research will include preparing and submitting research reports, publishing high-quality scientific articles, and participating in dissemination activities at the European level.
Required qualifications
Applicants must hold a master’s degree in Marine Technology, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a closely related field. Applicants must have their master’s thesis approved by the application deadline.

Applicants are expected to have in-depth knowledge of several of the following subjects:

• Marine hydrodynamics
• Structural Dynamics
• Physics-based simulations of marine structures
• Stochastic analysis methods
• Design optimization

• The average grade for courses included in the bachelor's degree (or equivalent) should be C (or equivalent) or higher. 
• The average grade for all courses (including the dissertation) in the master’s degree should be B (or equivalent) or higher. The master's dissertation (or equivalent) should have the grade B (or equivalent) or higher.

Application

jobs.occupation: Senior Platform Engineer (Kubernetes)
jobs.description:
About Six Robotics
At Six Robotics, we build intelligent software that gives Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) the ability to collaborate, adapt on the fly, and execute missions that were previously impossible. From our base in Oslo, our 70+ experts in defence, software, and AI develop our flagship autonomy and swarm platform used by both government and industry. In close partnership with the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI), we move fast from concept to live deployment, often in the field alongside end users.

We work with advanced hardware and software, a modern tech stack, and missions that demand both technical mastery and operational discipline. Everyone is close to the action, from deep technical problem-solving to field operations. We move fast and value clarity, integrity, and teamwork in everything we do.

At Six Robotics, every person executes with precision, adapts to changing conditions, and strengthens the team. Getting in is hard, and you’ll be challenged every day. But if you have the skill, the discipline, and the drive to push your limits and always be sharpening your blade, you’ll find no better place to deliver real-world impact while collaborating and learning from the best in the field.

About The Role
At Six Robotics, we know that achieving our mission requires more than great engineers; it requires an exceptional engineering environment. That’s where you come in.   We are building a self-hosted Kubernetes cluster that will serve as a multi-purpose platform for internal web services, CI runners, remote devcontainers, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) environments. This is not about maintaining an existing setup. It is about designing and implementing the foundation from scratch. 

Your mission follows this: to design, implement, and operationalize a highly available and scalable Kubernetes cluster that is adopted by developers and actively serving at least one of its intended purposes within the first six months. 

You will be part of Team Factory, which builds the internal infrastructure and tooling that engineering depends on. This is a role with real ownership, where there is room to become the key Kubernetes contributor in the company. 

What You Will Do
• 
Design and implement a highly available, self-hosted Kubernetes cluster

• 
Own cluster architecture, scalability, and lifecycle management

• 
Build a multi-purpose cluster supporting staging, production, CI runners, and remote dev containers.

• 
Develop internal tooling in Python and contribute to Kubernetes-specific components in Go where relevant

• 
Design resource-aware workload orchestration with priority- and capability-aware queueing mechanisms.

• 
Expose and integrate Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) setups into the platform

What we are looking for
We are looking for a Senior Engineer who understands Kubernetes beyond surface-level usage. You are comfortable operating between application developers and bare-metal infrastructure, and you proactively propose solutions rather than waiting for direction. 

You are motivated by ownership. You want to design something properly, build it, and maintain it over time. You thrive in environments where responsibility is real, and the technical bar is high. You think about how your technical decisions translate into value for real end users, and you are motivated by being part of building something that operates reliably in critical, real-world contexts where performance, correctness, and usability truly matter.

We believe the right candidate brings:
• 
5+ years of relevant experience in platform, infrastructure, or backend engineering

• 
Strong Kubernetes experience as a power user and at cluster-architecture level, not only deploying workloads

• 
Experience designing and operating self-hosted or on-prem Kubernetes environments

• 
Solid software engineering background and mindset, with comfort in languages like Python (for internal tooling) and Go

• 
Strong Linux fundamentals

• 
Experience with Docker and GitHub Actions

• 
Highly efficient and structured technical communication skills, expressing decisions and trade-offs in a clear manner

• 
Fluent in English (Norwegian not required)

Nice-to-haves:
• 
Experience with GitHub Actions Runner Controller (ARC)

• 
Dynamic VLAN configuration

• 
OpenStack

• 
Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) environments

• 
Building internal developer platforms

• 
Bare-metal-as-a-service concepts

• 
On-prem infrastructure management

Why You Should Join
At Six Robotics, we're not just building software - we're redefining how unmanned systems operate in the real world. If you're driven by meaningful problems, technical depth, and the chance to shape something from the ground up, you'll find your place here.

• 
Work on problems that matter

Our technology helps unlock smarter, safer, and more adaptable UAV operations in defense and industry, solving real challenges with direct, tangible impact.

• 
Lead the shift in a hardware-dominated space

We're bringing modern AI, autonomy, and scalable software into a field that's long relied on rigid, pre-programmed systems, to change how UAVs are designed, deployed, and managed.

• 
Build from zero, shape the future

Join early and help define the core systems, tools, and culture of a company that’s still being built - where your ideas, code, and decisions will have a lasting influence.

• 
Work with purpose, supported by great benefits You'll be part of a mission-driven team that values clarity, integrity, and collaboration, offering competitive pay, equity potential, strong insurance and pension plans, and ongoing learning opportunities.

Our Recruitment Process
• 
Screening interview with one of our recruiters to get to know you better (30 min).

• 
Meet & Greet with someone from the team to learn more about us (60 min).

• 
Programming assignment to be solved in your own time, followed by a technical interview more closely related to the specifics of the role (90 min).

• 
Final interview with our CTO and Head of People (45 min)

Reference check followed by an offer if everything goes well. We consider applications continuously, so don’t hold off with applying if this looks interesting. 

Our Commitment to Inclusion 

At Six Robotics, we are committed to creating a workplace built on respect, integrity, and collaboration. We value different perspectives and experiences, and we believe that diversity within our team strengthens both our work and our culture. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply and help us build technology that makes a real impact.

Security Clearance Requirement

All employees at Six Robotics are required to undergo a security clearance due to our close collaboration with the Norwegian Armed Forces. While prior clearance is not necessary, the clearance process will be initiated as part of onboarding.

Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network CAPTURE, collaborate with academic, healthcare, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on wireless endoscopy.

As part of the CAPTURE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting.

The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. The expected start date is 1 August 2027.

Your immediate leader will be the unit leader of Colourlab.
About the project
The CAPTURE project is an EU-funded Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network dedicated to advancing wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) through developments in computer vision and artificial intelligence. The project aims to improve image-based diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment by developing methods that reduce clinicians’ workload, enhance imaging quality, and support more accurate and timely diagnoses.

CAPTURE combines research with a strong focus on doctoral training, preparing a new generation of researchers to work at the interface of technology and medicine. The consortium brings together expertise from academia, industry, and hospitals, ensuring that the research is both scientifically rigorous and clinically relevant.

The project focuses on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), reflecting its growing prevalence in Europe. As many of the methods developed have broader applicability, the project will also consider other gastrointestinal diseases. These goals will be achieved through the recruitment and training of 15 doctoral candidates in an international and intersectoral environment, providing interdisciplinary expertise across the technical, clinical, and applied aspects of WCE.
Duties of the position
The WCEs currently applied for gastrointestinal imaging mainly contain RGB cameras. This is not necessarily optimal for imaging inside the gastrointestinal system.  

This project aims at studying multispectral imaging of the gastrointestinal system, enabling multispectral imaging capabilities for WCE. The focus will be on finding optimal spectral bands for relevant pathologies as well as efficient design of spectral imaging process.  

The goals for this PhD project are:   

• Determine the most suitable spectral bands for detection and classification of target pathologies under given resource constraints like sensor size, power consumption etc. 
• Investigate methods for improved pathology detection and visualisation for suggested multispectral approach.  
• Experimental verification of spectral bands using emulated capsule. 
This will include application of advanced hyperspectral equipment to measure target pathologies, construction of custom endoscope for experimental verification, as well as testing at Innlandet Hospital Trust.

Key responsibilities

• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate.
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above.
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination.
• Participate in the Colourlab research group.
• Participate in the network’s joint research and training activities, both online and in person across the CAPTURE partner institutions and contribute to CAPTURE project deliverables in accordance with the Description of Action and the project's governance procedures.
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to University of Thessaly in Greece and University of Granada in Spain.
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have solid experience with imaging or image processing. 
• You must have very good programming skills.
• At the date of recruitment, you must NOT have been awarded a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally been awarded the degree are also not eligible.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant master's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, imaging science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.

If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
• You must comply with the MSCA mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment (short stays such as holidays are not taken into account). 
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
Preference may be given to candidates with:

• Background in multi- or hyperspectral imaging.
• Experience with hardware and electronics in general.
• Excellent analytical and communication skills.
• Ability to work in an international and interdisciplinary environment.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to:  

• Work independently and in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals, and get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity, and be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
• Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject
• Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
 

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
• As an employee in Norway, the successful candidate will normally be a member of the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme, which provides access to public healthcare and social security benefits in accordance with applicable legislation and regulations.
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. This will cover the MSCA Living Allowance and Mobility Allowance. In addition, a family allowance may be provided in accordance with MSCA regulations.

A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary.

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Computer Science within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

The position is conditional on external funding.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The successful applicant must devote full working time to the project and the doctoral training programme.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request. Incomplete applications will not be prioritised.

The application must include: 

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• CV 
• Copy of master’s thesis. If you have recently submitted your master’s thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed master’s degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project and progress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages) 
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page)

•  Possibly certificates

If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

Evaluation processApplications will be assessed by an expert committee based on the qualifications and documentation submitted by the applicants. The evaluation will consider academic achievements, the quality and relevance of the applicant's educational background, research potential, and suitability for the position. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an interview. The final appointment will be made in accordance with the applicable regulations for employment at the university.

You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

jobs.occupation: Head of Laboratory
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the job
NTNU is the foremost technical university in Norway, located in Trondheim. NTNU NanoLab is a 700 m² cleanroom facility opened in 2009, and a central part of NTNU’s strategic initiative for Nanoscience, Nanotechnology and Functional Materials. The Faculty of Natural Sciences is the host faculty.

NTNU NanoLab is an open-access cleanroom serving both academia and industry, equipped for nano-structuring and characterisation using physical, chemical and biological methods. On average 300 users from diverse scientific fields use the facility each year. NTNU NanoLab is part of the Norwegian national infrastructure for micro- and nanofabrication (NorFab), the Nordic Nanolab Network (NNN) and the European cleanroom consortium EuroNanoLab. The permanent staff includes the Director, six service and process engineers, and the Head of Laboratory.

The Head of Laboratory is a technical administrator who acts as the leader of the engineering team and is the interface between our users, the University and the NanoLab. The engineers are the competence holders for the cleanroom and its instrumentation. The leader role requires in-depth knowledge of all aspects of running an advanced cleanroom infrastructure, including but not limited to chemical handling (toxic, explosive, and pyrophoric gases; nanoparticles), air filtration, gas supply systems, building management systems (BMS), and laboratory information management systems (LIMS) as well as advanced scientific equipment. Some prior experience in maintenance and repair of scientific instrumentation is therefore required.

We are a positive, international team with good opportunities for both professional and personal development. NTNU NanoLab operates as a dynamic environment with a flat hierarchy where every employee has a genuine impact on the operation.

Your immediate leader will be the Director NTNU NanoLab
Duties of the position
Job Description

The Head of Laboratory is responsible for administrating and managing the operation of NTNU’s cleanroom facilities and supporting infrastructure. The position works closely with the leader of Technical Operations and reports to the Director of NTNU NanoLab, who holds personnel responsibility. If the perfect candidate cannot be found, NanoLab would have to withdraw the position for further assessement. 

 

Responsibilities include:

• Main contact point for existing and prospective users, suppliers and administrative functions at the university. 
• Work management and coordination of a team comprising 6 engineers, 7 PhD duty workers and 7 student assistants
• Service management to ensure excellent service to all users of NTNU NanoLab
• Continual improvement of existing administrative and infrastructure routines, and development of new ones, to ensure an efficient and safe work environment
• Follow-up on routines and procedures established by engineers
• Development of pricing policy and coordination of invoicing routines with the finance department
• Contribution to development and implementation of the long-term investment plan
• Coordination of user training and overview of all cleanroom activities
• Coordination with NTNU and external vendors for service and maintenance of the infrastructure, and with internal and external users of NanoLab
• Promotion of NTNU NanoLab to increase utilisation of the infrastructure
• Representation of NTNU NanoLab at national and international networking meetings
• Coordination of investments and major cleanroom rebuilds
• HSE coordinator responsibilities in a challenging environment with over 300 users per year, involving use of dangerous chemicals and gases, and complex infrastructure
• Ensuring legal compliance across GDPR, export control, HSE, and other relevant regulations
• Administration of access control and the EQS deviation management system
• Supporting the NanoLab team whenever required.Required selection criteria
• Master’s degree in a relevant technical field
• 5–10 years of relevant work experience within a cleanroom fabrication environment
• Leadership experience or documented leadership competence
• Project management experience, including competence in managing investment processes through public procurement
• Proven experience of building or maintaining management systems that ensure consistent quality and continual improvement, grounded in the fundamentals of ISO 9001 - you will be structuring our all laboratory processes and helping maintain them together with the rest of the team
• Hands-on experience building/maintaining financial models (i.e. pricing)
• Experience with managing and structuring HSE work, especially pertaining to the use of dangerous chemicals in a multi-user environment. 
• Experience/certification for safe handling of dangerous gases
• Experience in service, repair, and maintenance of advanced scientific instrumentation 
• Knowledgeable on the fundamentals of ISO 9001 certification
• Good written and spoken Norwegian and English language competence is essential.Preferred selection criteria
• Customer service experience
• Familiarity with relevant software such as LIMS and project management tools
• Written and oral proficiency in Norwegian (to at least Level B2) and English – 
• Demonstrated ability to work in a dynamic environment with multiple deliverables and stakeholdersPersonal characteristics 
• The successful candidate is service-minded and solution-oriented, with a genuine drive to optimize and develop cleanroom operations and service quality. 
• You are self-driven and tenacious, with excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to maintain momentum through challenges. 
• You have a broad set of experience pertaining to the workings of a nanofabrication cleanroom infrastructure that allow you to assess the operations as a whole and then prioritize and focus your own and the teams efforts to provide the best level of service to our users.
• You have strong organizational skills and are structured, systematic, and detail-oriented, while remaining flexible enough to adapt to a dynamic work environment. Personal suitability is of high importance for this position.
In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal suitability, as well as motivation, in terms of the qualification requirements specified in the advertisement. 

If the perfectly suited candidate cannot be found, Nanolab would of safety reasons withdraw the position.
We offer
• exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment
• an open and inclusive work environment with dedicated colleagues
• favorable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• employee benefitsGeneral information 
NTNU believes that inclusion and diversity is a strength. We want our faculty and staff to reflect Norway’s culturally diverse population and we continuously seek to hire the best minds. This enables NTNU to increase productivity and innovation, improve decision making processes, raise employee satisfaction, compete academically with global top-ranking institutions and carry out our social responsibilities within education and research. NTNU emphasizes accessibility and encourages qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender identity, ability status, periods of unemployment or ethnic and cultural background.

The city of Trondheim is a modern European city with a rich cultural scene. Trondheim is the innovation capital of Norway with a population of 200,000. The Norwegian welfare state, including healthcare, schools, kindergartens and overall equality, is probably the best of its kind in the world. Professional subsidized day-care for children is easily available. Furthermore, Trondheim offers great opportunities for education (including international schools) and possibilities to enjoy nature, culture and family life and has low crime rates and clean air quality.

jobs.occupation: Professor or Associate Professor in Supply Chain Management
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus on professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sOm stillingen
Supply chains are at the core of industrial competitiveness, sustainability, and resilience. As industries face the twin transitions of digitalization and the Green Shift, advances in artificial intelligence, data analytics, and automation are creating new opportunities to transform how supply chains are designed, managed, and improved.

We are seeking an Associate Professor/Professor in Supply Chain Management to join the Production Management Research Group at the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MTP) at NTNU, an internationally recognized environment for research in production, logistics, and industrial systems. Supported by the state-of-the-art Logistics 4.0 Lab, the group conducts cutting-edge research in close collaboration with industry and leading international partners, with projects funded by the EU, the Research Council of Norway, and other major funding bodies. We are looking for an experienced researcher who can strengthen and expand our capabilities through research excellence, industry engagement, and external collaboration. You bring a strong understanding of industrial challenges and opportunities, enabling you to build meaningful partnerships and translate research into impact. Through your experience, professional network, and fresh perspectives, you will help shape new research directions, strengthen our collaboration with industry, and further develop our international standing. As part of our group, you will contribute to developing future engineers and managers capable of designing, implementing, and improving integrated supply chains that connect people, products, materials, information, technologies, and resources across the entire value chain.

Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering (MTP) at NTNU offers a vibrant and interdisciplinary research environment spanning logistics, production management, robotics, product development, materials science, and risk and reliability. We combine academic excellence with strong industrial relevance and are committed to fostering an open, collaborative, and inclusive community. The department offers education at all levels, from Bachelor's and Master's programs to PhD studies, within mechanical- management-, and industrial engineering, along with ICT. 

We welcome candidates who take a holistic and interdisciplinary approach to supply chain management, combining perspectives from industrial engineering and management, and decision science, with computer science, social science, natural science. Particular interest will be given to research addressing the role of emerging technologies, such as AI and digital technologies in enabling resilient, sustainable, circular, and high-performing supply chains that support the future of Norwegian and global industry, as well as their seamless integration in raw material sourcing, product development and supply chain design, and end-of-life product and material recovery and r-strategies.

Your immediate leader is Head of Department.
Duties of the position
• international level research in the scientific area of ​​supply chain management, resulting in publications in internationally top ranked journals in your field
• actively build and maintain industrial supply chain network in Norway  
• initiate new research projects through active interaction with industry and the funding bodies (e.g. EU and The Norwegian Research Council)
• initiate, participate in, and manage externally and internally funded research projects
• contributing to, fronting and leading the development of the research area within your field of research
• teaching at bachelor, master and PhD levels in all the study programs taught in the department
• supervision of bachelor, master and PhD students and provide mentorship to Postdocs and researchers
• contribute to the development and the activities of the Logistics4.0 Lab
• exam preparation and evaluation
• administrative tasks as requiredRequired qualifications 
You must have the qualifications required for the position of Professor or Associate Professor in the field of supply chain management, as outlined in the regulations concerning appointment and promotion to teaching and research posts.

To qualify for this Professor or Associate Professor position, we require the following:

• your academic research production must be within the field of supply chain management  
• you must have minimum 5 year of experience (after PhD) either from supply chain work in industry or research in academia
• you must document a track record of collecting external research  funding if your work experience is from academia
• you must have experience of applying qualitative methodologies, in particular case research, action research, conceptual modelling in supply chain management.
• you must have experience of applying quantitative methodologies, in particular analytical modelling and data-driven (AI-based) modelling, and knowledge in programming and simulation tools for supply chain management.
• you must have publications in highly ranked journals in your field. Scientific articles published in the last five years (excluding career breaks) with relevance for the research areas mentioned above and where interdisciplinary approaches are used will weigh strongest in the evaluation and ranking. The scientific publication record will be evaluated in light of the length of the applicant's academic career taking into account the research field.
• you must have documented experience as researcher/post-doc or equivalent.
• you must have documented experience at least in preparing research funding applications (EU level will be preferred) and you must show ability to define proper attractive research. For professorship position, you must have documented experience in successful funding applications and managing roles in research projects.
• you must have documented experience in teaching, supervising master students, and assisting the supervision of PhD students and you must show ability to define innovative teaching activities. For professorship position, you must have documented experience in supervising PhD students
• you must have collaboration experience with industry and/or public sector
• you need excellent oral and written English language skills
You must document relevant basic competence for teaching and supervision at university/higher education-level, ref. Regulations. If this cannot be documented, you are required to complete an approved course in university teaching within two years of commencement. NTNU offers qualifying courses.

New employees who do not speak a Scandinavian language by appointment is required, within three years, to demonstrate skills in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language equivalent to level three of the course for Norwegian for speakers of other languages at the Department of Language and Literature at NTNU. 
Preferred qualifications
• you should have international collaboration experience and an internationally oriented mindset
• you should have experience in participation in the development of educational materials
• you should have experience in designing and developing experimental research both in industrial context and laboratory environment
• you should be fluent in Norwegian (or Scandinavian) language for teaching and actively pursue network building in industry  Personal qualities
• high ambitions, both on behalf of your own achievements and those of colleagues
• reliable and respectful
• positive, curios and willing to learn, 
• self-motivated and motivational
• problem solver, systematic and systems-thinker
• willing to collaborate both within groups in the department and across NTNU
• able to work both independently and in a team
• willing to share results with colleagues locally and globally
• emphasis will be placed on personal and interpersonal qualities.
Emphasis will be placed on personal and interpersonal qualities.
We offer 
• a work environment for professional development as researcher and educator
• a world class infrastructure for research
• exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment
• an open and inclusive work environment with dedicated colleagues
• favored terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• employee benefitsApplication Process
You can find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.
Video: https://youtu.be/bwfNPj8HxHwSalary and conditions
In a position as Professor (code 1013) you will normally be remunerated from gross NOK 800000 to NOK 1000000 per year, depending on qualifications and seniority.

In a position as Associate Professor (code 1011) you will normally be remunerated from gross NOK 600000 to NOK 800000 per year, depending on qualifications and seniority.

As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants, and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU.  

After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.
About the application
Your application and supporting documentation must be in English.

Please note that applications are only evaluated based on the information available on the application deadline. You should ensure that your application shows clearly how your skills and experience meet the criteria which are set out above.

Length of the academic career will be considered in evaluating the application. If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result.

The application must include:

• CV, certificates and diplomas
• academic works - published or unpublished - that you would like to be considered in the assessment (up to 10 works - Joint works will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint works, you must attach a brief description of your participation)
• details of the projects you have initiated, participated in and managed, with information about funding, duration and size
• a description of the academic works that you regard as most relevant and that you particularly want to be considered in the assessment
• a description (maximum 3-5 pages) on how the candidate envisions her/his research in a Norwegian context and what would be the main sources of funding
• a description of the teaching activities that you regard as most relevant and that you particularly want to be considered in the assessment
• a description (maximum 2 pages) on how the candidate envisions her/his teaching activities in a Norwegian context
• name and contact details of three references
It is important that you both document and reflect on your competence. You are encouraged to use the NTNUs competence matrix as a guide for  documentation of your competence.

Joint work will also be considered. If it is difficult to identify your specific input to a joint project, you must include evidence of your contributions.

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Our assessment of the pedagogical skills will be based on documented pedagogical material, forms of presentation in your academic works, teaching experience, PhD, and Masters supervision, and any other relevant pedagogical background. Both quality and scope will be taken into consideration, and an open scientific practice will be recognized.

NTNU is obliged by the evaluation criteria for research quality in accordance with The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment – DORA and the obligations in the Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment ( CoARA) on responsible assessment of research and recognition of a wider range of academic contributions to science and society. This means that we will pay particular attention to the quality and academic range demonstrated by your scientific work to date. We will also pay attention to research leadership and participation in research projects. Your scientific work from the last five years will be given the most weight.

Your application will be considered by an expert committee. Candidates of interest will be invited to an interview, and to deliver a trial teaching session.
General information
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals.

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.  

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 

---------------------

The city of Trondheim is a modern European city with a rich cultural scene. Trondheim is the innovation capital of Norway with a population of 200,000. The Norwegian welfare state, including healthcare, schools, kindergartens and overall equality, is probably the best of its kind in the world. Professional subsidized day-care for children is easily available. Furthermore, Trondheim offers great opportunities for education (including international schools) and possibilities to enjoy nature, culture and family life and has low crime rates and clean air quality.

----------------------

As an employee at NTNU, you must continually maintain and improve your professional development and be flexible regarding any organizational changes.

A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you want to reserve yourself from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality.

Finnsnes ligger i Senja kommune i Troms i Nord-Norge og er et viktig transport- og regionsenter i Midt-Troms. Området byr på spektakulær nordnorsk natur, samtidig som Finnsnes har et aktivt næringsliv og gode servicetilbud.

In ENGLISH:

Professional Drivers Wanted – Bus, Minibus, Truck.

Location: Finnsnes, Troms, Northern Norway

Ulf Trulsen AS, Senja Tours and Finnsnes Termotransport are looking for skilled and reliable professional drivers to join our operations in Finnsnes.

We are looking for

• Bus drivers – Category D for coach/tour bus and passenger transport

• Minibus drivers – Category D1

• Truck drivers – Category C/CE for freight transport, distribution and long-haul transport

Flexible shift and rotation schedules

We offer several work arrangements and aim to find a solution that suits each individual driver:

• Full-time positions with regular working hours

• 14/14 rotation – 14 days working / 14 days off

• Monthly rotation – one month working / one month off

• Other rotation schedules by agreement

Our rotation schedules are particularly suitable for drivers who wish to commute between their home country and Norway, while enjoying longer periods of time off.

Accommodation and housing

We can assist drivers who wish to relocate to Norway in finding accommodation in the Finnsnes area.

For drivers who prefer to commute, we can also look into affordable accommodation during working periods, such as:

• Rooms

• Apartments

• Modular accommodation

• Other suitable housing solutions

Our goal is to make it as easy as possible to combine working with us with living and family life in your home country.

We help you with the transition to Norway

For candidates from the Nordic countries and EU/EEA, we can provide guidance and practical assistance with matters related to starting work in Norway, including:

• Driving licences and Driver CPC / YSK

• Norwegian rules and requirements

• Tax registration

• Housing and accommodation

• Other practical and administrative matters

We assess each candidate individually and aim to find good solutions regarding work arrangements, rotation schedules, accommodation and commuting.

About Finnsnes

Finnsnes is located in Senja Municipality in Troms, Northern Norway, and is an important transport and regional centre in Mid-Troms. The area offers spectacular Northern Norwegian nature, while Finnsnes has an active business community and good local services.

We are looking for someone who

• Holds a Category D, D1, C or CE driving licence, depending on the position

• Holds the required Driver CPC / YSK

• Is a safe and responsible driver

• Is service-minded and professional

• Works well independently and is flexible

• Speaks Norwegian (or another Scandinavian langiage) and/or English

Previous professional driving experience is an advantage.

Interested?

Please send us your CV and a short introduction about yourself. Let us know which driving license category you hold, what type of driving you are interested in, and whether you are looking for a full-time position, rotation work or a commuting arrangement.

We welcome qualified drivers from Norway, the Nordic countries and the EU/EEA to apply.

Location: Finnsnes, Troms, Norway

Positions: D / D1 / C / CE

Work arrangements: Full-time and various rotation schedules

Start date: By agreement

jobs.occupation: Head of Sales (Nordics)
jobs.description:
About Us
At No Isolation, we’re a profitable, 65-person Norwegian EdTech scale-up operating across Europe. We help educators bring learning and belonging to every child.

Our AV1 robot is deployed in 19 countries, with 5,000+ units supporting schools to improve attendance, belonging, and continuity of learning for children who cannot be physically present. Consistently described as life-changing, it bridges the gap between the student and their peers, restoring both educational continuity and the essential sense of social belonging.

We’re established enough to have a proven solution and strong financial foundations, yet still small enough for every new colleague to have a visible impact on our next stage of growth.

The Opportunity - Head of Sales, Nordics
You’ve led sales teams selling to kommuner and other public sector clients. You know how to multi-thread across multiple stakeholders, navigate decision and budget processes, and like being hands-on the most important of deals. Now you want a new challenge with a strong team to develop, and a solution customers actually need and want.

The Nordics are our home market - with some of our best market penetration, where customers rarely churn, yet with lots of market opportunity still to capture. We’re looking for someone who will lead from the front and help a small team across Norway, Sweden and Denmark drive our growth.

What your week looks like
• 
Joining your Account Managers in their customer meetings and helping them close.

• 
Deal reviews and pipeline check-ins with the team.

• 
Working with Marketing, Product and Customer Success on what’s coming next.

• 
Attending and speaking at industry events where our customers are.

What you’ll own
• 
Your own portfolio of key municipal and education accounts, from first meeting to signed agreement.

• 
The move from single-school sales to framework agreements with kommuner and education authorities.

• 
The team’s results across three markets that each need their own plan.

• 
Where we focus: which segments, territories and accounts are worth the push.

• 
A pipeline and forecast in HubSpot that you’re happy to stand behind.

You are probably someone who
• 
Has a track record leading B2B/B2G sales teams - ideally has sold to Norwegian kommuner or other public sector clients, and knows how budgets, politics and procurement work. Experience from other Nordic countries or the Baltics is a plus.

• 
Until recently carried a quota, and/or has remained heavily involved in shaping and closing deals yourself.

• 
Has led and coached account managers, and knows that different people need different support to improve and perform their best.

• 
Understands the importance of sales methodologies, whether that’s MEDDPICC, SPIN, Challenger or similar.

• 
Is data driven and uses CRM (HubSPot a plus) to understand trends and drive performance.

• 
Speaks fluent Norwegian and English. Swedish or Danish is a bonus.

• 
Is based in Oslo and happy with a hybrid setup.

Who you’ll work with
You’ll report to our CCO, Sanjeev, who is based in London and previously led Vodafone business units across Africa and Europe. From our Oslo HQ you’ll work closely with our CEO, Morten, a former McKinsey Partner, and an experienced Leadership Team.

What’s in it for you
• 
Real earning potential. We offer uncapped commission beyond OTE. The need is high and the solution proven - it now requires someone to drive systematic execution.

• 
A solution that sells. It’s unique, backed by evidence of impact and significantly more cost-effective compared to alternatives. Our churn is very low - the solution works and customers love it.

• 
Something to build on. You’re taking over a successful team that now needs taking up to the next level.

• 
A place people like working. Our engagement scores are above benchmark, and we have structured onboarding with a buddy, an annual company trip and great collaboration across teams.

• 
Enhanced parental and sick leave.

• 
Flexible hours around a 10:00–15:00 core, with the option to work remotely.

• 
Central office in Oslo.

• 
27 vacation days.

• 
Travel insurance for you and your immediate family.

• 
Mobile phone and internet subscription.

Location
This role is based in our Oslo HQ office, with regular travel across Norway, Sweden and Denmark to support your team in the field.

We believe in-person leadership matters, so we work a flexible hybrid model built around real collaboration.

How to Apply
Please click Apply and upload your CV in English.

If you’d like, you can also include a short video (in English) as part of your application – this is optional, but it gives us a chance to see a bit more of who you are beyond your CV. Let your personality and passion shine!

If you're looking for a leadership role where the demand is already proven and the job is to build on that - not create it from scratch - we'd love to hear from you.

🎥 You can watch how AV1 transforms inclusion in education here: vimeo.com/1098745115

🌍 You can explore our mission and impact stories at noisolation.com

We kindly ask external recruitment agencies and consultants to refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

Om arbeidsgiveren:
We help educators bring learning and belonging to every child.

School absence is the biggest challenge facing education. Our AV1 robots connect absent students, ensure learning and belonging, and support reintegration back to the classroom.

Today, there are over 3,500 active AV1 robots used across 18 European countries. Positioned in the EdTech sector, AV1 is a unique solution to the growing issue of persistent absence, supporting both the academic and social needs of students.

No Isolation works across Europe, with 45 employees across Europe and in offices in Oslo, Munich and London. Join us in our growth journey!

jobs.occupation: St. nr. 11/2026 - PhD Position in Mathematics Education, Artificial Intelligence and Competence Dev
jobs.employer_name: HØGSKULEN I VOLDA AVD FOR HUMANISTISKE FAG OG LÆRERUT
jobs.description:
The position
Faculty of Humanities and education, The Department of Science and Mathematics at Volda University College invites applications for a three-year PhD Position in mathematics education, artificial intelligence (AI) and competence development.

The position is linked to research activities within TRUST (The Norwegian Centre for Trustworthy AI), one of Norway’s national research centres for artificial intelligence. 

The successful candidate will apply for admission to the PhD programme in Education, Language and Culture at Volda University College. The programme takes an interdisciplinary approach, incorporating perspectives on teaching and learning across different subject areas.

The PhD project will be developed in close collaboration with the supervisors within the research framework outlined in this announcement. The candidate is expected to start as soon as possible after appointment.
The research project
Artificial intelligence is transforming education, working life and society, creating a need for new knowledge about the competencies people require in an AI-rich society. The project focuses particularly on mathematical competencies relevant to the development, use and understanding of AI, including modelling, abstraction, statistical reasoning and algorithmic thinking.

The candidate will develop an independent doctoral research project within this broad framework. Possible areas of investigation may include:

• which mathematical and AI-related competencies will become important in a society shaped by AI
• how such competencies are integrated into education and can be developed through educational practice
• how teaching approaches, learning resources and initiatives for competence development can be designed
• how such initiatives can be investigated and evaluated in authentic educational settings
• how AI may shape students’ opportunities for mathematics learning, academic support and developing life skills across home, school and everyday settings
• how these changes may help reduce social and educational inequalities and support participation and democratic development
The project will be rooted in mathematics education research. The final research questions, theoretical framework and research design will be developed in collaboration with the supervisors.

Through TRUST – The Norwegian Centre for Trustworthy AI, and its more than 70 national and international partners from academia, industry, government, and civil society, the candidate will have access to an extensive national and international research network.

TRUST is advancing trustworthy AI that is accurate, interpretable, inclusive, fair, safe, sustainable and well governed. Combining expertise in (i) machine learning, statistics, mathematics, and data science, (ii) law, and social sciences, and (iii) philosophy, the centre develops AI technologies and interdisciplinary frameworks, supports innovation and examines AI’s impact on democracy, the rule of law, and the environment. Research spans theoretical, methodological, legal and empirical perspectives, tested in real-world contexts, including healthcare, mobility, governance, security, and climate resilience. Users, citizens and civil society organisations contribute to assessing the trustworthiness of research and innovation. 

TRUST is funded by the Research Council of Norway and public and private partners, and is led by the University of Oslo, SINTEF and the Norwegian Computing Center (NR). 
Responsibilities
The candidate will:

• carry out an independent doctoral research project
• plan and conduct research activities and data collection
• analyse research data and publish findings
• disseminate research through academic publications, conferences and other relevant forums
• participate actively in the research community at Volda University College and in TRUST-related activities
• collaborate with national and international research partners and practitionersRequired qualifications
Applicants must have:

• a master’s degree or equivalent qualification in mathematics education, mathematics, computing education, educational sciences or a closely related field
• an academic background qualifying for admission to the PhD programme in Education, Language and Culture at Volda University College, normally with grades equivalent to B or higher
• good spoken and written English skills
Desirable qualifications

We particularly welcome applicants who can demonstrate one or more of the following:

• documented competence in mathematics teaching or mathematics education, for example through teaching, research, development work or teacher education
• documented knowledge of or experience with AI, digital technology, programming, data analysis or related areas
• competence in mathematical modelling, statistics or statistical analysis
• experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research methods
• research experience in mathematics education, educational sciences or a related field
• familiarity with the Norwegian or another Scandinavian education system, curriculum development or competence development
Proficiency in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language is an advantage, particularly for collaboration with schools, data collection and research dissemination, but is not a requirement.

Personal qualities

We are seeking a candidate who:

• is intellectually curious and motivated to undertake doctoral research
• works independently and systematically
• has strong collaboration and communication skills
• is motivated and committed to contribute actively to an interdisciplinary research environment
Personal suitability will be taken into account.
We offer
• a fully funded three-year PhD position
• an active community of doctoral candidates affiliated with the PhD programme in Education, Language and Culture
• a strong research environment in science, mathematics, and mathematics education at Volda University College
• participation in research activities and networks associated with TRUST
• excellent opportunities for national and international research collaboration
• salary in accordance with the Norwegian state salary scale and membership of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK). The starting salary is set at NOK 580,000, with an automatic annual progression of 3% for a maximum of 4 years.General information
Volda University College is committed to diversity and encourages qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, disability, or ethnic background.

The appointment will be made in accordance with the terms and conditions applicable to the position. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview.

Applications must be submitted electronically via Jobbnorge. A public list of applicants will be drawn up after the application deadline. Applicants who wish to request exemption from the public list must provide reasons for this in their application.
 Application requirements
Applications must include:

• a cover letter and a statement of motivation (1–2 pages) explaining the applicant’s motivation and how their academic background and expertise are relevant to the position
• a curriculum vitae (CV)
• degree certificates and academic transcripts
• a writing sample, such as a master’s thesis, manuscript or published article
• the names and contact details of 2–3 referees 
The PhD project will be developed in collaboration with the supervisors after appointment.

Applications may be written in English, Norwegian, or another Scandinavian language.
Contact
For further information about the position, please contact:

• Arve Fiskerstrand, Associate Professor, Department of Science and Mathematics, arve.fiskerstrand@hivolda.no
• Andreas Brandsæter, Professor, Department of Science and Mathematics, andreas.brandsaeter@hivolda.noStudiebygda Volda

Høgskulen i Volda er høgskulen for humaniora og samfunnsvitskap i Møre og Romsdal. Vi er ein spennande kompetanseorganisasjon i vekst med om lag 4500 studentar og 380 tilsette. Vi gjev undervisning i ei rekkje fagområde, yrkesretta utdanningar og etter- og vidareutdanningar i nært samarbeid med samfunns- og næringsliv. Høgskulen i Volda driv mykje forsking og utviklingsarbeid og satsar på forskaropplæring og kompetanseoppbygging for dei tilsette i samarbeid med universitet i inn- og utland.
