Om stillingen
Universitetet i Stavanger har ledig stilling som stipendiat i flerspråklighet og tverrspråklig påvirkning ved Fakultet for utdanningsvitenskap og humaniora, Institutt for kultur- og språkvitenskap. Stillingen er ledig fra 01.03.2027

Stipendiatstillingen leder fram til doktorgrad og gir deg mulighet til å utvikle forskningskompetanse i et aktivt og stimulerende fagmiljø. Gjennom doktorgradsutdanningen opparbeider du kunnskap, ferdigheter og erfaring som kvalifiserer for videre karriere innenfor forskning, høyere utdanning og andre kunnskapsintensive sektorer.

Den som ansettes tas opp på doktorgradsprogrammet i utdanningsvitenskap og humaniora. Programmet omfatter blant annet selvstendig forskningsarbeid, deltakelse i nasjonale og internasjonale forskermiljø, samt forskningsformidling. Les mer om forskerutdanningen ved UiS på våre nettsider.
 
Stillingen er for tre år med ren forskerutdanning, eller fire år med forskerutdanning kombinert med annet karrierefremmende arbeid. Dette avklares i rekrutteringsprosessen.

Som stipendiat ved UiS får du støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling gjennom veiledning, kompetanseutvikling og karriereplanlegging.
Forskningstema
Den som ansettes vil være tilknyttet forskergruppen FLUENT (Flerspråklig Utvikling og Endring i Nyere Tid) og Institutt for kultur- og språkvitenskap. FLUENT forsker på flerspråklighet fra ulike perspektiver, inkludert tilegnelses-, formelle og utdanningsvitenskapelige perspektiver. Forskergruppen er tverrfaglig og åpen for ulike teoretiske og metodiske tilnærminger.

Denne stipendiatstillingen er en åpen utlysning for doktorgradsprosjekter innen flerspråklighet, med særlig fokus på tverrspråklig påvirkning (cross-linguistic influence, CLI) hos to- og flerspråklige talere. Målet er å bidra til økt forståelse av hvordan språk påvirker hverandre i flerspråklige språksystemer, og i hvilken grad grammatiske systemer deles mellom språk.

Selv om tverrspråklig påvirkning er et veletablert fenomen, er det fortsatt mye vi ikke vet om hvilke faktorer som påvirker denne prosessen. Særlig er det behov for mer kunnskap om hvordan språkenes egenskaper og den språklige avstanden mellom dem har en effekt på tverrspråklig påvirkning. Videre er det behov for mer forskning på hvordan ulike typer flerspråklige talere (for eksempel barn og voksne, tidlige og sene tospråklige) og individuelle faktorer som språkferdighet, eksponering og språkbruk påvirker slike prosesser. Fordi mye av tidligere forskning har basert seg på offline- metoder, som for eksempel grammatikalitetsvurderinger, vet vi relativt lite om hvordan tverrspråklig påvirkning kommer til uttrykk mens flerspråklige talere prosesserer språk i sanntid.

Doktorgradsprosjektet skal bidra med ny empirisk kunnskap om tverrspråklig påvirkning ved hjelp av offline-, online- eller kombinerte metodiske tilnærminger. Søkere oppfordres til å utvikle sitt eget prosjekt innenfor dette brede forskningstemaet.

Mulige tema for doktorgradsprosjektet inkluderer, men er ikke begrenset til:

• i hvilken grad tverrspråklig påvirkning varierer som følge av språklig avstand mellom språk
• i hvilken grad tverrspråklig påvirkning varierer mellom ulike språklige nivåer, som syntaks, morfologi, ordforråd og fonologi
• i hvilken grad tverrspråklig påvirkning varierer mellom ulike typer flerspråklige, for eksempel barn og voksne, tidlige og sene tospråklige eller tredjespråksinnlærere
• i hvilken grad individuelle faktorer, som språkferdighet, språklig eksponering og språkbruk, påvirker tverrspråklig påvirkning
• i hvilken grad tverrspråklig påvirkning kommer til uttrykk på samme eller ulike måter i flerspråkliges språklige kunnskap og i språkprosessering i sanntid 
Prosjekter kan omhandle et bredt spekter av språkkombinasjoner. Prosjekter som inkluderer norsk i kombinasjon med ett eller flere andre språk er særlig relevante, men også andre språkkombinasjoner er velkomne. Stavangers flerspråklige befolkning gir gode muligheter for rekruttering av deltakere med ulike språkbakgrunner.

Avhandlingen skal skrives på engelsk.
Prosjektskisse
Som søker skal du utarbeide en foreløpig prosjektskisse for et doktorgradsprosjekt innenfor det beskrevne forskningstemaet.

Prosjektskissen skal redegjøre for prosjektets problemstilling, relevans, samt teoretisk og metodisk tilnærming. Prosjektskissen, som bør være på ca. 4-5 sider, vil inngå i kompetansevurderingen. 

Dersom du blir ansatt, vil prosjektskissen og prosjektets framdriftsplan videreutvikles i samarbeid med veilederne i løpet av de tre første månedene av ansettelsesperioden og danne grunnlag for den endelige planen for doktorgradsprosjektet. Mal for prosjektskisse finner du her. Prosjektskissen skal skrives på engelsk.
Kvalifikasjoner
Du må ha en sterk faglig bakgrunn med femårig mastergrad innenfor språkvitenskap (linguistics), flerspråklighet, psykolingvistikk, anvendt språkvitenskap, nordisk språk, engelsk språk eller tilsvarende utdanning som gir grunnlag for å gjennomføre en forskerutdanning, fortrinnsvis av nyere dato.

Karakter på masteroppgaven og veid gjennomsnittskarakter for masterstudiet må begge tilsvare B eller bedre. 

Dersom du har utdanning fra en institusjon med annen karakterskala enn A-F, ber vi deg legge ved dokumentasjon som viser hvordan karakterene kan sammenliknes med den norske karakterskalaen. Du kan bruke disse konverteringsskalaene til å beregne poengene dine for opptak.
 
Vi legger også vekt på at du:

• har interesse for forskning på flerspråklighet, språktilegnelse og/eller språkprosessering 
• har erfaring med språkvitenskapelig forskning og gjerne eksperimentelle eller kvantitative metoder
• har høy faglig integritet og fokus på kvalitet i arbeidet
• er nysgjerrig og motivert for å gjennomføre forskningsprosjektet og bidra til faglige fellesskap og samarbeid på tvers av fagområder
• har potensial for forskning innenfor fagfeltet og personlige forutsetninger for å fullføre doktorgradsutdanningen innen ansettelsesperioden
• kan arbeide godt både selvstendig og i samarbeid med andre forskere
• har evne til kritisk refleksjon, nytenkning og selvstendig problemløsning, og arbeider strukturert og målrettet
• har gode samarbeids- og kommunikasjonsevner og bidrar til et konstruktivt arbeidsmiljø.
• har gode ferdigheter i engelsk, både skriftlig og muntlig.Krav til engelskkunnskaper
Gode ferdigheter i engelsk, både skriftlig og muntlig, er en forutsetning for opptak til doktorgradsprogrammet. 

Dersom du er internasjonal søker og ikke omfattes av fritaksordningene nedenfor, må du dokumentere engelskkunnskapene dine med et gyldig resultat fra én av følgende språktester:

• TOEFL – Test of English as a Foreign Language, Internet-Based Test (IBT). Minimum resultat: 90/4.5
• IELTS – International English Language Testing Service. Minimum resultat: 6.5
• Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) eller Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE) fra Universitetet i Cambridge
• PTE Academic – Pearson Test of English Academic. Minimum resultat: 62
Du er fritatt fra kravet dersom du:

• har fullført minst ett års universitetsstudier i Australia, Canada, Irland, New Zealand, Storbritannia eller USA
• har fullført en mastergrad med engelsk som undervisningsspråk i et EU-/EØS-land eller i India
• er fritatt i henhold til HK-dirs GSU liste
• ikke inngår i de ovennevnte unntakskategoriene, men har bodd i Norge de siste fem åreneSom stipendiat ved UiS får du
• forskerutdanning ved et universitet med et viktig samfunnsoppdrag
• et ambisiøst og inkluderende forskningsmiljø
• veiledning og støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling
• gratis norskkurs dersom du ikke behersker norsk, svensk eller dansk på minimum A2-nivå ved ansettelse
• tilgang til Lifekeys, en digital tjeneste for mental helse og livskvalitet
• lønn som stipendiat etter Statens lønnsregulativ i stillingskode 1017, kr 580.000 brutto pr år, med lønnsutvikling etter ansiennitet i stillingen. 
• medlemskap i Statens pensjonskasse med gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger
Les mer om ansattgoder og fordeler på uis.no.
Mangfold og inkludering
Mangfold er en styrke ved universitetet. Ulike erfaringer, perspektiver og bakgrunner bidrar til bedre løsninger og et godt arbeids- og læringsmiljø. Vi ønsker søkere med ulike kvalifikasjoner, livserfaringer og perspektiver, og oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke, uavhengig av kjønn, alder, funksjonsevne, kulturell bakgrunn eller om du har hatt opphold i arbeidslivet. UiS legger til rette for ansatte i ulike livsfaser og for medarbeidere med behov for individuell tilrettelegging. 
 
I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.  
Har du spørsmål?
Ta gjerne kontakt dersom du ønsker å vite mer om stillingen og prosjektbeskrivelse:

• Førsteamanuensis Brechje van Osch, e-post: brechje.a.osch@uis.no 
• Førsteamanuensis Yvonne van Baal, e-post: yvonne.w.vanbaal@uis.no .
Har du spørsmål om ansettelsesprosessen, kan du kontakte: 

• HR- rådgiver Christine Valvik., tlf: 51 83 24 23, e-post: christine.valvik@uis.noSlik søker du
Søk stillingen ved å klikke på "Søk stillingen" på denne siden. 

I Jobbnorge registrerer du søknad, relevant utdanning og arbeidserfaring samt språkferdigheter. I søknaden ber vi deg beskrive dine forskningsinteresser, din motivasjon for stillingen og hvordan din bakgrunn er relevant for forskningsprosjektet.

Følgende dokumentasjon skal lastes opp som vedlegg til søknaden:

• prosjektskisse, se mal tilgjengelig på våre nettsider
• CV med fullstendig oversikt over utdanning, erfaring og eventuell vitenskapelig virksomhet
• vitnemål med karakterutskrift som dokumenterer fullført mastergrad. Dersom du ikke har fullført mastergraden, skal du legge ved oppdatert karakterutskrift.
• Diploma Supplement eller tilsvarende dokumentasjon, samt konverteringsskala dersom dette er påkrevd
• dokumentasjon på engelskspråklig kompetanse dersom dette er påkrevd
• publikasjoner eller annet relevant forskningsarbeid
• attester og annen dokumentasjon som vurderes relevant for søknaden 
Dokumentasjonen må foreligge på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. 

Søknaden vurderes på grunnlag av informasjonen som er registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristen utløp. Sørg derfor for at søknaden tydelig viser hvordan din kompetanse og erfaring oppfyller kompetansekravene i utlysningen, og at nødvendig dokumentasjon er lastet opp. Dersom vedleggene samlet overskrider 100 MB, må filene komprimeres før opplasting.

UiS behandler bare søknader og vedlegg registrert i Jobbnorge.

Opplysninger om søkere kan bli offentliggjort selv om det er bedt om unntak fra offentlig søkerliste, jf. offentlighetsloven § 25. Dersom anmodningen ikke tas til følge, vil du bli varslet.
Ansettelsesvilkår og videre prosess
UiS er underlagt sikkerhetsloven, og det forventes at ansatte utviser sikkerhetsbevisst atferd, og følger gjeldende sikkerhets- og eksportkontrollrutiner. Ved ansettelse vil egenskaper som pålitelighet, dømmekraft og lojalitet bli vektlagt.

Ansettelse som stipendiat er regulert i universitets- og høgskoleforskriften kapittel IV. Opptak til doktorgradsutdanningen er regulert i forskrift for graden philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) ved Universitetet i Stavanger.

Dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen vil bli vurdert av en intern komité på grunnlag av dokumentasjonen registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristens utløp. På bakgrunn av komiteens vurdering vil aktuelle søkere bli invitert til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser for aktuelle kandidater. Les mer om ansettelsesprosessen på våre nettsider.
 
Doktorgradsarbeidet skal i hovedsak gjennomføres ved Universitetet i Stavanger. Det er en forutsetning at den som ansettes bosetter seg slik at vedkommende kan være til stede og tilgjengelig for fagmiljøet i ordinær arbeidstid.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den norske teksten som legges til grunn.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Universitetet i Stavanger (UiS) har omlag 12.000 studenter og 1.900 ansatte. Universitetet har store ambisjoner. Vi skal ha en innovativ og internasjonal profil og være en drivkraft i kunnskapsutviklingen og endringsprosesser i samfunnet. Vår felles retning skal drives frem av omtanke for bærekraftig omstilling og rettferdig samfunnsutvikling, gjennom nye måter å forvalte naturressursene på og legge til rette for bedre byer og lokalsamfunn. Energi, helse og velferd, læring for livet er våre satsingsområder.I samspill og dialog med våre omgivelser regionalt, nasjonalt og internasjonalt har vi et åpent og innovativt klima for utdanning, forskning, kunstnerisk utviklingsarbeid, nyskapning, formidling og museumsvirksomhet. Den faglige virksomheten ved universitetet er organisert i seks fakultet med 13 institutt og to nasjonale forsknings- og kompetansesenter i tillegg til Arkeologisk museum. Vi er medlem i det europeiske nettverket for innovative universitet - European Consortium of Innovative Universities. Universitetet ligger i den mest attraktive regionen i landet med 300.000 innbyggere.  Stavangerregionen har et dynamisk arbeidsmarked og tilbyr en rekke spennende kultur- og fritidsaktiviteter.Sammen med våre ansatte og studenter vil vi løfte blikket, og våge å tenke stort og nytt – vi vil utfordre det velkjente og utforske det ukjentee.

 

Fakultet for utdanningsvitenskap og humaniora er regionens viktigste institusjon for utdanning av lærere til barnehage, grunnskole, videregående skole, høyskole og universitet. Fakultetet tilbyr også grunnutdanning innenfor idrett, språk, religion, historie, samt åtte masterprogrammer og en doktorgradsutdanning. Fakultetet har tre nasjonale sentre: Nasjonalt lesesenter, Nasjonalt senter for læringsmiljø og atferdsforskning (Læringsmiljøsenteret) og Kunnskapssenter for utdanning (KSU), samt forskningssentrene Filiorum - Senter for barnehageforskning og Greenhouse – Centre for environmental humanities. I tillegg er fakultetet en av fem universitetspartnere i Senter for spesialpedagogisk forskning og inkludering (SpedAims). Fakultetet samarbeider med Utdanningsdirektoratet, kommuner og fylkeskommuner om etter- og videreutdanning av ansatte i barnehage, skole og PPT. Fakultetet har ca. 3.300 studenter, og ca. 400 ansatte fordelt på fakultetsadministrasjonen, Institutt for barnehagelærerutdanning, Institutt for grunnskolelærerutdanning, idrett og spesialpedagogikk, Institutt for kultur- og språkvitenskap, Nasjonalt lesesenter, Læringsmiljøsenteret og Kunnskapssenter for utdanning.Institutt for kultur- og språkvitenskap har ansvar for universitetets lektorutdanning for trinn 8-13 og praktisk-pedagogisk utdanning. Instituttet tilbyr også utdanninger innenfor nordisk, engelsk, religion, historie, norsk for internasjonale studenter, og mastergradsutdanninger i historie og historiekultur, nordisk og lesevitenskap, samt engelsk og Literacy Studies. I tillegg har instituttet ansvar for det tverrfakultære årsstudiet Filosofi, politikk og økonomi (PPE), det engelskspråklige masterprogrammet Public Environmental Humanities og et deltidsstudium i museumspedagogikk. I samarbeid med andre enheter ved fakultetet tilbys doktorgradsutdanning i utdanningsvitenskap og humaniora. Det er i dag ca. 70 ansatte og ca. 800 studenter tilknyttet instituttet.

jobs.occupation: Research assistants in VaccAI and CuratedAI at MediaFutures
jobs.employer_name: UNIVERSITETET I BERGEN FAKULTETET FOR NATURVITENSKAP OG TEKNOLOGI
jobs.description:
UiB Knowledge that shapes society
UiB shall be among Europe’s leading universities, internationally recognized for high quality in research and education. As a societal institution, we shall contribute to sustainable and democratic development and be an attractive and inclusive place to study and work.
Video: https://youtu.be/M5n6RnScNgAResearch assistants 
There are two research assistant vacancies linked to VaccAI and CuratedAI at the Department of Information Science and Media Studies, University of Bergen, in the MediaFutures research environment. The positions will support research led by Professor Christoph Trattner.

• VaccAI: one 40% position starting as soon as possible after the application deadline of 15 November 2026, by agreement, and ending on 30 September 2028.
• CuratedAI: one 30% position starting as soon as possible after the application deadline of 15 November 2026, by agreement, and ending on 30 September 2028.
Research assistant is a recruitment position supporting academic staff in their teaching and research. The positions provide an opportunity to gain insight into scientific work and methodology. Total employment as a research assistant cannot exceed two years.
About the projects
VaccAI is a Research Council of Norway funded project examining vaccine related claims in the news and the information environment surrounding vaccination. The project combines analysis of news content with research on how people encounter and evaluate health information. Research assistants will help prepare and analyse research material and support empirical studies of vaccine communication and AI assisted approaches to assessing claims.

CuratedAI is a Research Council of Norway funded project examining artificial intelligence and transparency in journalism. It investigates how the use of AI in producing and verifying news can be communicated to audiences, and how transparency measures affect their understanding and evaluation of news. The research includes AI disclosure, provenance and watermarking approaches, and the needs of journalists and the public.

About MediaFutures

MediaFutures is a Centre for Research based Innovation hosted by the Department of Information Science and Media Studies at the University of Bergen, with its primary workplace at Media City Bergen. In collaboration with news media and technology partners, the centre develops responsible media technology and investigates media experiences, recommender systems, content production and analysis, and audience interaction. Read more at www.mediafutures.no.
Work tasks
The research assistants will formally report to the PI of the two projects Professor Christoph Trattner and support the relevant project teams in scientific, technical and project related administrative tasks. Tasks may include:

• Preparing, collecting, cleaning and documenting research data, including news content, survey responses and experimental data.
• Programming research tools, setting up study infrastructure and supporting online surveys and experiments.
• Reviewing literature, annotating research material and assisting with quantitative or qualitative analyses.
• Contributing to research documentation, reports, publications and dissemination activities.

A research engineer (spesialingeniør) position in molecular and cell biology is available in the research group targeted therapies and immunomodulation headed by Prof. Mouldy Sioud, Department of Cancer Immunology, Institute of Cancer Research, Oslo University Hospital-Radiumhospitalet.

The research group focuses on the development of new cancer therapeutics such as antibodies, antibody derivatives, and modified mRNA cancer vaccines using in vitro screening platforms and cell and molecular techniques. jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Societal readiness for AI-supported Life Cycle Assessment of buildings
jobs.employer_name: NTNU FAKULTET FOR ARKITEKTUR OG DESIGN
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

A PhD position in Societal readiness for AI-supported life cycle assessment in the architecture, engineering, and construction sectors is now open at the Energy and Environment Group at the Department of Architecture and Technology, NTNU. The Energy and Environment Group lead centres/projects like the Research centre on zero emission neighbourhoods in smart cities (ZEN), syn.ikia – Sustainable plus energy neighbourhoods, and the Green Deal ARV project on Climate positive circular communities. We use real demonstration projects and our laboratory facilities (like the ZEB laboratory) extensively in our research. The group currently comprises 10 senior staff members (professors and associate professors), and around 20 research fellows (research assistants, PhD candidates, and post-doctoral researchers). The duration of the position is 3 years.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
Life Cycle Assessment is a key instrument for environmental governance in the architecture, engineering, and construction industry. At the same time, new artificial intelligence (AI) based tools are beginning to automate central parts of the LCA-based design practice. This includes data gathering, model construction, scenario generation, results interpretation, and decision support. This development may increase speed and usability, especially in early-stage design, but it also raises important questions about transparency, methodological integrity, accountability, professional judgement, and institutional preparedness. 

This PhD project will examine the societal readiness of the architecture, engineering, and construction sectors for AI-supported environmental assessments. The use of AI-supported LCA tools will be studied through case applications, including usage of machine-learning approaches, large language models, and automated workflows. The project will analyze how such tools reshape trust, responsibility, accountability, and professional judgement in environmental decision-making, by adopting a mixed-method approach.

The project will be carried out at the Department of Architecture and Technology at NTNU, in cooperation with SINTEF Industry, department of Manufacturing and NTNU Social Research.

The immediate leader is head of department. The place of duty is Trondheim.
Duties of the position
• Carry out research of high quality on AI-assisted LCA in-light of applied use, environmental governance challenges, and societal readiness.
• Publishing in high-quality peer reviewed journals and popular science dissemination.
• Participate in the Energy and Environment research group at the Department of Architecture and Technology.
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions.
• Complete academic training consisting of coursework corresponding to a minimum of 30 ECTS
• Career-enhancing work, which is in addition to the research project and doctoral education, may be offered to a candidate who demonstrates clear motivation and ability for such work, and if the Department determines there is a need. Examples of career-enhancing work include, but are not limited to, contributing to teaching, laboratory and exercise teaching, supervision, and examination work within the employee's areas of competence. Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the doctoral program in architecture, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in Architecture, Industrial Ecology, Science and Technology studies, Computer Science, or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than November 1st, 2026.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• Excellent written and oral English language skills.
• Strong analytical skills and capabilities, proven through courses and/or thesis deliverables.
• Motivation to work on the selected topic.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Competence in Life Cycle Assessment and/or other environmental sustainability analysis methods.
• Previous relevant experience with use of Artificial Intelligence (e.g., large language models, machine learning, etc.), especially for Life Cycle Assessment or carbon accounting.
• Good programming skills in one or several languages (e.g., Python, MATLAB, R, etc.).
• Previous experience with relevant concepts from Science and Technology studies (such as co-production) will be seen in a positive light.
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian/Scandinavian language(s).Personal characteristics
• Strongly motivated to work on the topic.
• The successful candidate will become part of a multidisciplinary research environment. The candidate is expected to embrace this setting and be a true team player.
• Self-driven with a strong ability to work independently and maintain good structure and discipline in their work. 
• Demonstrated integrity and a strong sense of responsibility in their research conduct.
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
Evaluate and remove/add what is relevant for the position.

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2).
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Architecture within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information

If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Associate Professor Jan Sandstad Næss (email: jan.s.nass@ntnu.no). If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Advisor Natalia Swahn (email: Natalia.swahn@ntnu.no).

The attachments (including a description of scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Therefore, make sure that the application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. jobs.description:

Digitalization and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming society, and the integration of AI into the maritime industry represents a digital shift that will redefine today’s operations. The maritime industry is increasingly embracing AI, enabling a broad digital transformation. At the same time, the use of AI introduce new cybersecurity challenges that need to be understood and addressed to enable secure and trustworthy AI technology.

This PhD project will investigate cybersecurity challenges associated with the development and use of AI in the maritime domain. The project will have an interdisciplinary approach, combining insights from information security, artificial intelligence, maritime operations, and data engineering. The research may address cybersecurity risks related to the data used to develop AI models, the models themselves, or their integration and use in maritime applications.

Relevant research topics may include cybersecurity risks related to training data and AI models, data poisoning and manipulation, privacy and confidentiality, secure data sharing, and methods for assessing the security and trustworthiness of maritime AI technology. The specific research questions and methodological approach will be further developed based on the candidate’s background and interests, relevant maritime AI use cases, and collaboration with industry partners.

This position offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of cybersecurity, AI, and maritime operations in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners. The research is expected to contribute new knowledge and approaches for understanding and addressing cybersecurity challenges associated with the development and use of AI in the maritime domain.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.

The candidate will work in a multidisciplinary research environment located at the heart of the maritime industry in Ålesund. Working at the NTNU department of ICT and Natural Sciences ensures close contact with the industry and research communities.

The PhD project will be part of the Norwegian Maritime AI Center that aims to accelerate operationalization of AI in the maritime value chains. The center shall position the maritime sector for accelerated and successful use of AI. The demand for safe and sustainable maritime activities, as well as the shortage of crew and engineers, are key drivers for change in the maritime sector. At the same time, there is a pull for growth, increased efficiency and profitability, while managing volatility in the markets. Moreover, the sector is critically important for global supply chains and security in a tense geopolitical situation. To demonstrate and prototype maritime AI solutions, the center will address a diverse and impactful set of use cases: Logistics, shipping and business transactions; Ship design and construction; Voyage planning and optimization; Condition monitoring and maintenance; Crew training; Maritime traffic and ship surveillance; Decarbonization and energy management; Autonomous ships and remote control.

The research partners are the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), University of Oslo, Oslo School of Architecture and Design, Royal Norwegian Naval Academy, Norwegian Mapping Authority, MET and SINTEF Nordvest. There are about 30 user partners from the maritime sector, in addition to hundreds of members of the Maritime Forum, Blue Maritime, Ocean Autonomy, and Maritime CleanTech clusters. The center will be a hub, orchestrating the interfaces with research partners and user partners to facilitate collaboration, knowledge creation, dissemination, innovation, and sharing of knowledge. The Norwegian Maritime AI Center is funded by the Research Council of Norway and the partners for the period 2026-2030. There will be approximately 25 doctoral scholarships and some postdoc positions. More information can be found here: https://www.ntnu.edu/mai

3-year 100% PhD position is available at the Department of Pediatric Research, OUS Rikshospitalet for a highly motivated and skilled PhD student on a project funded by South-Eastern Norway Regional Health Authority. The position is available from 23rd November 2026.

Neonatal cholestasis is a condition with impaired bile flow causing accumulation of bile acids and bilirubin, liver damage and debilitating pruritus. Reduction in bile to the intestine results in malabsorption, reduced weight gain, vitamin deficiency and changes in microbiota. Both genetic and environmental factors can result in cholestasis.

About the Department / Research Group

Professor Runar Almaas (Pediatric hepatology) at PFI, OUS is leading the project. The PhD candidate will be supervised by him and by Co-supervisor Barbora Smolkova (PhD) and senior researcher Gareth Sullivan. The group is using induced pluripotent stem cells for making liver organoids and a major part of the work will be related to this model.
Oslo University Hospital is a workplace with great diversity. We believe this is crucial for solving our tasks in the best possible way. We want this diversity to be reflected among the applicants for our positions, and we encourage all qualified candidates, regardless of background, to apply!
Duties and responsabilities
What Tasks and Responsibilities Are Associated with the Position?

To reveal mechanisms of cholestasis and pruritus and to investigate novel potential treatments we are using liver organoids derived from disease-specific induced pluripotent stem cells. iPSC-derived liver organoids are a unique model that can mimic key features of the human liver and can be used to study liver development and disease. In these project liver organoids will be used for studying protein trafficking, effect of modulating factors and potential drugs.

jobs.occupation: Renovasjonssjåfør
jobs.description:
NordRen AS department Asker

We are looking for:

• Motivated individuals who are solution-oriented, have experience driving a truck and enjoy being physically active while working. You must enjoy working outdoors, regardless of weather conditions.

• Hold a valid Class C driving licence and a valid Driver CPC/CAP (Code 95). Be ready to operate our truck with precision and responsibility.

• Is in good physical shape and can work efficiently. We value a structured approach to work and the ability to handle tasks in an organized manner.

• We believe in service with a smile! We are looking for candidates with a positive attitude who value customer service and are ready to represent NordRen AS in a professional way.

• Can take initiative, work independently, and are proactive in handling various tasks.

• Good language skills in English. You must be able to participate in an online interview in English.

• Digital skills – Comfortable using maps on a tablet in the trucks.

Work tasks:

• Collection and transport of household waste on established routes. With maps on pad in the trucks. 

• Responsibility for the truck, including weekly washing and weekly/daily maintenance according to routines.

• Monitoring of waste sorting and discrepancy recording.

• Communicating with and guiding customers when necessary.

• Other tasks typically associated with the waste collection profession.

We offer:

• Environmentally conscious: NordRen AS is committed to contributing to a sustainable future. As one of Norway's leading companies in waste management, we are proud of our environmental focus and our commitment to waste sorting.

• Secure workplace: Join a company that has experienced steady growth since its establishment in 2013. NordRen AS offers you the opportunity to help shape the future of waste management.

• Performing a socially beneficial and socially critical service.

• Gain valuable experience in handling challenging situations in traffic.

• Varied workday.

• 7.5-hour workday during daytime (06:00-13:30) Rotational work or shift work is not possible.

• Secure job with Class C License.

• Annual salary from NOK 516 750- 528 450, - (€ 48 249 – 49 342) depending on experience. 

• NordRen covers further education (35 hours) related to CPC. 

• NordRen can help with accommodation for a period 3-6 months. (Considering the location and working   hours, having your own car is an advantage.)

• NordRen covers Norwegian language courses (A2) after 3 months of employment. 

How to apply:

Send CV and application letter to: rekruttering@nordren.no. 

Please mark the application with Department Asker

Om arbeidsgiveren:

In NordRen departement Asker, we have 23 trucks. Some are small Volvo and Iveco single-operator trucks, while the larger ones are Scania three-axle trucks with two-person crews. The trucks have two compartments: One for paper and one for plastic, one for food and one for residual waste.

Each two-person crew handles between 300 and 350 stops per day, meaning they empty around 600–700 bins daily. All bins are equipped with RFID chips, which are scanned by antennas on the lifting mechanism during collection. This records the chip number, time of collection, and waste type and kilos of waste

We empty approximately 1.8 million waste containers on an annual basis.

On average, we empty about 7000 - 7500 containers per day, totaling around 36 000 containers per week.

jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Risk-Based Power System Operation and Utilisation of Transformer Capacity
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? Do you have a background in electric power systems and are you interested in risk-based power system operation? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia. 

The Department of Electric Energy (IEL) at NTNU is seeking a highly motivated candidate for a full-time (100%) PhD position for 3 years in “Risk-Based Power System Operation and Utilisation of Transformer Capacity”. You will join the research group Power System Operation and Analysis (PSOA) at IEL, where we foster an open, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.

Our working environment is characterized by a friendly, supportive atmosphere, with regular gatherings such as professional meetings within the research group, weekly research colloquia, shared lunches, and “Friday coffee” sessions to wrap up the week. Formal and informal gatherings provide opportunities to exchange ideas, celebrate milestones, and strengthen connections. PhD Candidates also arrange social activities, open to everyone who wishes to join, creating a welcoming and inclusive community.

Your immediate Line Manager will be the Head of Department.
About the project
The PhD position is a part of the Knowledge-building Project “Increasing Emergency Load Limits for Transformers” (KSP UPLOAD) that is starting up in 2027. SINTEF Energy Research is the project owner.  NTNU is a participating partner, together with leading industry partners. Hiring for the PhD position is subject to the final confirmation of funding availability from KSP UPLOAD.

Liquid-immersed power transformers are critical power grid assets. Due to an ageing power grid, growing demand for electricity, and very long lead times on installing new transformers, there is a need to both increase the utilization of existing infrastructure of transformers and to maximise the value of new investments. Increasing the short-term load limits for transformers will free up capacity to accommodate new load and generation, reduce the need for reinvestments, and provide back-up capacity in case of emergency. Improved methods for condition monitoring and prediction, along with better risk criteria can reduce uncertainties and offer a possibility for increasing the transformer loading. KSP UPLOAD will investigate key failure mechanisms for transformers, map the benefits and risks of increasing the load and temperature limits, and pilot new concepts for risk control. 

The PhD Position belongs to Work Package 1 of KSP UPLOAD: ‘System-level Benefits and Risks in from Increased Loading’. It addresses the question of how to quantify the socio-economic benefits, as well as the risk with respect to reliability of supply, when operating transformers beyond nameplate limits. 

The tasks meant for the PhD work are related to:  

• Quantifying how higher loading limits affect the socio-economic trade-off between reliability of supply and making additional capacity available to power markets with flow-based market coupling.
• Developing methods for optimally allocating the additional transfer capability enabled by increased transformer loading limits across day-ahead, intraday, and balancing markets to maximize socio-economic value while respecting system security and reliability constraints.
Different approaches can be explored, such as integrating probabilistic and deterministic reliability criteria with market operation in a single security-constrained optimal power flow model, and combining optimal power flow analysis with reliability analysis methods.

The main supervisor of the PhD Candidate will be Associate Professor Vijay Venu Vadlamudi (IEL). Co-supervisors will be Professor Hossein Farahmand (IEL) and Senior Research Scientist Iver Bakken Sperstad (SINTEF Energy Research). 
Duties of the position
• Conduct high-quality research within the framework described above.
• Participate in activities of the research group Power System Operation and Analysis (PSOA).
• Complete academic training consisting of coursework corresponding to a minimum of 30 ECTS.
• Contribute to publications in relevant journals and to popular science dissemination.
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions.
Career-enhancing work, which is in addition to the research project and doctoral education, may be offered to a candidate who demonstrates clear motivation and ability for such work, and if the Department determines there is a need. Examples of career-enhancing work include, but are not limited to, contributing to teaching, laboratory and exercise teaching, supervision, and examination work within the employee's areas of competence. 

Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must hold a Master’s degree within Electric Power Engineering, with specialization in electric power and/or energy systems. 
• Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at the Master's level. Master's students can apply, but the Master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position, and no later than autumn 2026.
• You must have proficient programming skills in Python.
• Employment is contingent upon the candidate’s ability to obtain the required security clearance.
• You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education, i.e., by having relevant work experience and/or published/publishable scientific papers.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the Faculty's Doctoral Programme.
• You must have English language skills, both written and spoken, corresponding to the scale B2 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). Applicants who are not native English speakers are encouraged to document their English language proficiency. One of the following test scores could be documented for this purpose: 
• TOEFL internet-based test (iBT) - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 79 - 101. 
• IELTS - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 5.5 - 6.0 
• Cambridge English - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 160 - 179.
Further assessment of both written and oral English language skills and the ability to communicate fluently will be conducted in the continued selection process and during any interviews for all applicants.

PLEASE NOTE: For detailed information about what the application must contain, see paragraph “About the application”.

The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Master’s thesis relevant to the announced position.
• English language skills, both written and spoken, corresponding to the scale C1 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). See which scores are equivalent to the C1 level here.
• Proficiency in a Scandinavian language (Norwegian, Swedish, or Danish), both written and spoken, at B2 level or higher is considered an advantage. The candidate is expected to collaborate with stakeholders in the Norwegian industry and utility sectors, where Norwegian is the working language.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• demonstrate strong motivation, curiosity, and a learning-oriented mindset
• work independently, take initiative, and maintain good structure and discipline in their work
• communicate effectively and collaborate well with supervisors and peers
• show resilience and work constructively when facing challenges or setbacks
• demonstrate integrity and a strong sense of responsibility in their research conduct
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period

The Shipping Management program is part of the Maritime Operations team, combining education and research across both shore and sea —at both operational and managerial levels. Digital transformation is changing the maritime industry and the relationship between shore and sea, and brings new requirements for business models, roles, responsibilities, and competence. Our research in particular focuses on how new maritime technologies and environmental regulations affect maritime operations. jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow position in Knowledge-Grounded LLM Agents for Defensive Cyber Operations
jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a PhD Research Fellow position in Knowledge-Grounded LLM Agents for Defensive Cyber Operations, available at the Digital Security Research Group within the Department of Informatics at the University of Oslo.

Starting date as soon as possible and no later than 01.05.2027. The fellowship period is three years.

A fourth year may be considered, which would involve 25% other career-promoting work. Other career-promoting work may consist of teaching, supervision, and/or research assistance. This depends on the applicant's qualifications and the department's current needs.

No one can be appointed for more than one PhD Research Fellowship period at the University of Oslo.
Project description
The position will investigate knowledge-grounded and neuro-symbolic approaches to large language models and agentic AI for defensive cyber operations. The PhD project will be carried out in close collaboration with the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI), including co-supervision from FFI with potential to connect the research to relevant cybersecurity and cyber-defence challenges.

The research will explore how heterogeneous cybersecurity intelligence and evidence sources, including telemetry and observations, can be transformed into structured cybersecurity knowledge, represented through semantic knowledge graphs, and combined with symbolic reasoning, modern language models, and autonomous agents to support security analysis, situational awareness, decision-making, and response. Particular emphasis will be placed on developing trustworthy, reliable, interpretable, and secure AI systems, including methods for grounding, reasoning, validation, and the control of agentic behaviour in security-critical environments. 
 
The security and robustness of LLM-based and agentic systems, including adversarial manipulation, uncertainty, provenance, and the validation of AI-generated decisions and actions, may also be explored as part of this position.
What skills are important in this role?
The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences has a strategic ambition to be among Europe’s leading communities for research, education and innovation. Candidates for these fellowships will be selected in accordance with this, and expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials.

Required qualifications:

• Master’s degree or equivalent in cybersecurity, computer science (informatics), artificial intelligence, or a closely related field. Foreign completed degree (M.Sc.-level) corresponding to a minimum of four years in the Norwegian educational system
• Strong foundation in computer science or artificial intelligence/machine learning, with knowledge of cybersecurity or a demonstrated motivation to apply AI/ML in cybersecurity
• Strong programming and software development skills, demonstrated through relevant projects, research, or equivalent experience
• Fluent oral and written communication skills in English
Candidates who have not yet completed their master’s degree must have completed all requirements for the degree by 31.12.2026.

The position will involve cooperation with stakeholders related to Norwegian national security, and candidates' suitability for this will also be taken into account.

Desired qualifications:

• Knowledge of or experience with large language models (LLMs), agentic AI, and related AI/ML methods
• Knowledge of or experience with semantic technologies, including knowledge graphs, ontologies, knowledge representation, and/or symbolic reasoning
• Knowledge of or experience with cybersecurity, particularly cybersecurity operations, security analysis, threat detection and response, cyber threat intelligence, or security automation
• Knowledge of or interest in trustworthy and secure AI, including robustness, interpretability, validation, uncertainty, or the security of LLM-based and agentic systems
• Previous research experience, for example, through a master’s thesis, scientific publication, research project, or equivalent work, is considered an advantage
Language requirement:

• Good oral and written communication skills in English
• English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/ EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements:https://www.mn.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/regulations.html#toc8
Grade requirements:The norm is as follows:

• The average grade point for courses included in the Bachelor’s degree must be C or better in the Norwegian educational system
• The average grade point for courses included in the Master’s degree must be B or better in the Norwegian educational system
• The Master’s thesis must have the grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system
For more information see:

The purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. 

UiO is subject to the Security Act, which governs the organisation's protection of security-sensitive objects and knowledge, in addition to other relevant legislation concerning access to and handling of sensitive information. Based on this, it is a requirement that successful applicants are security-eligible. We may use background checks as part of our recruitment process.
What are we looking for in you?
Personal skills:

• Ability to work independently and take initiative, while also contributing effectively to collaborative research
• Analytical, critical, and structured approach to research and problem-solving
• Curiosity and willingness to learn, with the ability to adapt to new research questions, methods, and technologies
• Good communication and collaboration skills, and the ability to engage constructively in interdisciplinary research
• Positive attitude and the ability to handle hectic periods
Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal qualifications.
We can offer you
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organisation with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development
• Committed colleagues in a good working environment
• Good welfare schemes
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours
• A workplace with good development and career opportunities
• Career development programmes
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes
• Oslo’s family-friendly surroundings with their rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities
• Salary in position as PhD Research Fellow, position code 1017 in salary range NOK from 550 800 - 595 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund We need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

How to apply
The application must include:

• Transcripts of records, copies of the original Bachelor’s and Master’s degree diplomas (see below)

jobs.occupation: Position(s) as Associate Professor in Accounting
jobs.description:
About the position
Oslo Business School is a relatively new business school (founded in 2014) focusing on teaching quality and excellence in research. The school has currently about 2000 students and 80 employees and offers study programs at Bachelor, Master, and PhD level. The Finance and Accounting group, one of the school’s five sections, is a vibrant and diverse group consisting of researchers that regularly publish in recognized international journals. Oslo Business School is located in downtown Oslo and is part of the Oslo Metropolitan University. The school is currently working on obtaining international accreditations and is strongly focusing on enhancing research output in high quality journals. 

Oslo Business School is expanding and invites applications for 1-2 faculty positions in accounting. The positions are within the Finance and Accounting group, and the person(s) appointed will contribute to Oslo Business School's research and teaching in accounting and auditing and related subjects. The formal recruitment will be at the associate professor level with tenure. Candidates who qualify may be promoted to full professor following their appointment.
Your main duties and areas of responsibility will be
• teaching and supervision at the Bachelor, Master, and PhD level 
• active contribution to the development of a high-quality education 
• initiating and carrying out high quality academic research 
• contributing to the continued development of the research group in accounting and auditing and the department’s study programmes 
• academic-administrative tasks 
• active contribution to the development of Oslo Business School, and OsloMet in general 
• disseminating research outcomes to the academic community and to the broader societyQualification requirements
The ranking of qualified applicants is based on scientific merits. Teaching experience, personal qualities and suitability for the position are also important factors. We mainly consider recent publications and the potential for future publications in high-quality journals. The candidates we hire should fit the profile of our bachelor and master programs and must be able to contribute to the school’s long-term academic development. We encourage women to apply.

Applicants must:

• hold a PhD in accounting or related fields (or be close to completion) 
• have published in international journals and/or document the potential for quality publications in accounting 
• have good teaching skills 
• written and oral proficiency in Norwegian, Swedish or Danish (minimum level B2), and English (Language requirements for employees at OsloMet)
Applicants who do not have adequate proficiency in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language, will be offered Norwegian courses, and must acquire Norwegian skills corresponding to at least level B2 within three years of appointment.

The applicant must document relevant educational competence in accordance with OsloMet’s Guidelines for the assessment of educational competence at OsloMet. Applicants who do not possess the required educational qualifications must obtain them within two years of employment.

General criteria for appointments to academic positions are covered by the Regulations for appointment and promotion to academic posts.
It will be an advantage if you have
• high quality research in recognized international journals
• experience with research networks and externally funded projects
• teaching and supervision experience from different degree levels
• quantitative skills, related to empirical research or teaching
• proficiency in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language
• capability in communicating and cooperating with students and colleagues
• a relevant professional credential (such as statsautorisert revisor)
• ability to teach Norwegian accounting standards (GRS norsk regnskapslov)
• personal qualities that contribute positively to the working environmentPersonal qualities
OsloMet evaluates teaching qualifications in conjunction with interviews. It is important for OsloMet to reflect the population in our region, and all qualified candidates are welcome to apply. We make active endeavours to further develop OsloMet as an inclusive workplace and to adapt the workplace if required. If there are periods where you have not been in work, under education or in training, you are also welcome to apply.
We offer
• engaging professional opportunities at Norway’s third largest university
• an exciting job opportunity at a new and fast-growing business school in the middle of downtown Oslo 
• participation in a dynamic professional environment, research groups, and unique academic community
• a possibility to help map out the direction of a new and growing business school
• opportunities for academic development in a professional research environment
• interaction with a diverse student group
• loan and pension arrangements through the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund 
• beneficial welfare schemes and a wide range of sports and cultural offers
• free Norwegian language classes to employees 
• working location in downtown Oslo with multiple cultural offers
The salary for the position is in accordance with the Basic Collective Agreement for state employees and OsloMet’s pay policy for Associate Professor in code 1011, corresponding to 708 000 – 923 000 NOK per year. A higher salary may be considered for particularly well-qualified applicants. The salary depends on the qualifications of the applicant. From the salary, 2% will be deducted in pension contributions for the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK).
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SHi5avzdHIkApplication Process and Expert Committee
If you wish to apply for the position, you must do so through our recruitment system.An expert committee will conduct the assessment of relevant applications. Before the application documents are sent to the expert committee, all applications will be reviewed by the faculty. Applications from unqualified candidates will not be forwarded to the expert committee for assessment. If the number of applications requires it, an internal screening committee at OsloMet will carry out an initial selection of candidates. The selected applicants will then be assessed by the expert committee. 

Please upload the following documents by the application deadline: 

• application letter 
• CV, letters of recommendations, and all pages of certificates/diplomas. Foreign education should be pre-approved, and a letter of approval must be attached. Information is available via the following link: Recognition of foreign education - to work in Norway | HK-dir 
• a list of scientific publications/working papers 
• up to 5 scientific publications (from the last five years), including your PhD thesis 
• documentation of educational competence including a profiling document
For applicants who cannot document the required competencies in teaching in higher education have to develop this within two years from accession. OsloMet offers courses in teaching and learning in higher education which covers this requirement.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
The Department of Biology (IBI) at NV faculty has a vacant 3-year PhD position for a marine macroalgae research in the Marine Sciences section  The position is part of a NTNU well known niche nationally using enabling technology for research and education of algal (phytoplankton, ice algae, macroalgae) dynamics to provide knowledge needed for better ecosystem function and management. This position will be shared with researchers at Department of Biotechnology and Food Science (IBT) focusing on biochemistry (also at NV faculty at NTNU). In addition, the PhD will also collaborate with SINTEF Industry (Department of Biotechnology and Nanomedicine) focusing on industrial applications. 

The overarching aim of the Marine Sciences section is focused on sustainable management, production, and utilization of biological marine resources. The announced position will be important in utilizing the momentum in educating the next NTNU generation of marine scientists using enabling technologies to understand, monitor and improve ecosystem health including reduction of human induced stress in the environment. Our departments do work with industry to find solutions and enhance the understanding of ecosystem function to utilize resources in a benign manner to provide “good ecology = good economy”.

The PhD candidate will be part of the EU Horizon project “Restoring ocean and waters in waterfront cities and their ports”. The specific objectives are to 1) protect and restore marine and freshwater ecosystems and biodiversity, 2) prevent and eliminate pollution of our ocean, seas and waters and 3) make a blue economy sustainable, carbon neutral and circular.

In Trondheim, our major environmental challenge is sewage and industry wastewater discharge into the Trondheimsfjord, inducing multiple stressors for marine production and biodiversity. Cascade effects, including replacements of kelp species with filamentous algae (“turf”), loss of fish and poor water quality.

Remedies approach: Restore declining population and habitats, including cultivation of kelp to remove excessive nutrients, heavy metals and provide biomass for products in the new blue economy. Our goal is to contribute to reduced pollution, better restoration, maintenance of biodiversity and improved water quality.

The main activities for the PhD will be to contribute to ensure habitat functions in macroalgae along coastal areas near Trondheim (restoration) which also include cultivation of seaweed at sites with different degrees of pollution level (e.g. nutrient loads and heavy metals). Identification, mapping and monitoring macroalgal growth zones and key environmental variables such as light, temperature, salinity, nutrient loads (e.g. nitrate, phosphate, silicate) by using different robotic platforms (using the operation pyramid comprising mini satellites, aerial drones, autonomous surface and underwater vehicles and moorings) in collaboration with Applied Underwater Robotic laboratory (NTNU) and Fjordlab (part of Ocean Space Centre in Trondheim of (NTNU & SINTEF) will be carried out.

The seaweed elemental composition will be analyzed for using cultivated seaweed as bioindicators (uptake of nutrients and pollutants), and biorefinery, including product development, for selected applications will be part of the project.

The hired candidate will be able to join a dynamic, cross-disciplinary team that is working on the development of new techniques to provide ecological, physiological and biochemical information needed for enhanced environmental monitoring and corresponding industrial applications.

The primary workplace will be at the Trondheim Biological Station, but changes in the place of work may occur during the project period.

Your immediate leader will be the head of the department of Biology.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Provide time-series of Key Environmental Variables (KEV) in Trondheimsfjord and corresponding growth dynamics of selected macroalgal species comprising brown, red and green macroalgae
• Model species for natural habitats and growth cultures will be the kelp species Saccharina latissima and Alaria esculenta and the brown wreck Fucus vesiculosus
• Combine information on elemental composition and ecophysiology (eg. photosynthetic parameters and pigment composition) in model species to use the algae as bioindicators of water quality and habitat stress level
• Chemical characterisation of seaweed biomass (cultivated, from restoration areas and from wild populations)
• Development of sequential biorefinery on cultivated biomass (several end-products for increased valorisation)
• Separation of heavy metal rich fractions from biomass 
• Communicate with stakeholders along the entire cultivation seaweed value chain and stay updated on national/international regulations (monitoring, restoration)
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in marine biology, biochemistry or biotechnology for ecological or biochemical studies of marine micro- and/or macroalgae. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• You must have hands on experience with methods for in in situ and laboratory methods/observations to measure phytoplankton/macroalgal biomass and health status with focus on one/several topics related to biodiversity, biochemical composition, primary production and function)
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works
• Excellent written and oral English skills
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• A MSc with experience from cross disciplinary work using enabling technology for marine ecology
• Experience in algal systematics, pigment and sugar chemistry, statistics methods, user/making codes in R or Python
• Experience using of underwater mobile platforms (e.g. pilot experience using Remotely Operated Vehicles) is beneficial
• Experience with seaweed hatcheries and cultivation
• Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian/Scandinavian equivalent level A2Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are/have: 

• Hands on and highly motivated to use your PhD project as a contribution for a better marine nature management locally and internationally (core of Remedies project)

jobs.occupation: Hardware Reliability Manager
jobs.description:
Nofence is a Norwegian scale-up that has built the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock. As we aim to revolutionize livestock management, we need top-notch competence in our Engineering team, and we are now looking for an Hardware Reliability Manager for our Hardware Reliability Team.

Hardware Reliability Team
Our Hardware Reliability Team works with quality at both ends of our product life cycle. First: Validation of new livestock product designs, and second: monitoring and identifying failures on products in the field. These tasks are split into two disciplines: validation and failure analysis. As Hardware Reliability Manager, you will lead both of these teams. You will have a holistic view of the real-life conditions of our products, and ensure that these conditions are replicated in the lab. What can not be replicated in the lab has to be validated in the field on test farms around the globe. You will also monitor product performance, coordinate field investigations, and recommend mitigations of quality issues together with other stakeholders.

Your main responsibilities will be:
• 
Shape the overall validation and quality strategy to match business goals and risk tolerance.

• 
Lead the Hardware Reliability Team across new and existing products - setting priorities, allocating resources across projects, clearing roadblocks, and keeping the team on track.

• 
Deliver clear, structured reporting on test progress, pass/fail metrics, and overall quality status.

• 
Own end-to-end mechanical, electronics, and embedded validation plans from early product development through mass production and failure analysis.

• 
Serve as a service point for internal stakeholders on validation and product quality.

• 
Plan, conduct, and execute field testing under real-world operating conditions to validate product performance and catch issue trends early.

• 
Monitor collar performance in the field after we release the product.

• 
Coordinate validation activities delivered to the engineering and manufacturing teams.

We are looking for someone who has:
• 
Bachelor or Master degree in engineering or another relevant degree

• 
Experience with leading engineering activities within hardware and software

• 
Experience with leading cross-functional teams at a technical level

• 
Excellent analytical skills

• 
Proven project management skills

• 
Knowledge of international testing standards

We are looking for someone who is:
• 
Motivated by working in an autonomous cross-functional team.

• 
Thrives in a fast-paced development environment and can rapidly assess and prioritize critical issues.

• 
Structured with the ability to bridge the gap between engineers and internal and external stakeholders.

• 
Willing and able to travel across the Nordic region and internationally to meet with end-users and colleagues.

• 
Comfortable working in an English-speaking environment.

About Nofence
Managing livestock has always been a challenge. Humanity has tried everything from herding with dogs to walling the animals in with barbed wire, electric, and wooden fences, but these are costly and time-consuming solutions and often in conflict with the local wildlife. It has also left vast areas of potential pasture overgrown and underutilized.

Until now.

Enter virtual fences. What started as a small group of farmers and engineers with a big idea has become Nofence – the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock.

What we bring to the table
At Nofence, we're not your typical 9-to-5 gig. We're a dynamic scale-up, creating a work atmosphere that's anything but ordinary. It's a place where dedication and innovation are the norm, offering great opportunities for your personal and professional growth.

We believe in seeing results fast. As a manager, your work won't be lost in the bureaucratic shuffle. You'll witness the immediate impact of your contributions in real-time, influencing the evolution of our cutting-edge virtual fencing solution for livestock.

Join us, where ambition meets reality, and let's keep pushing the boundaries in the world of agri-tech!

About the Application

In line with applicable data protection regulations and our data protection practices, we are unable to accept or process applications received by email. Applying through the portal also ensures your personal data is handled securely. We will evaluate candidates continuously and look forward to hearing from you! If you have any questions about Nofence or the application, please reach out to our VP Engineering Fabien Lepoutre at below email.
